lead: Stricter rules put an end to greenwashing. But is that enough? In Het Debat, Barend den Heijer of Marcel's Green Soap and Hiske Arts and Femke Sleegers of Fossielvrij Nederland write about the next step.

lead: Ilse DeLange (49) has warm memories of the Eurovision Song Contest, but would she want to represent the Netherlands again? On 'Eva' the singer says she is a lot less sure about that these days.

lead: A photo taken from a distance of American president Donald Trump in his plane has sparked renewed speculation about the Kennedy Center. It shows Trump looking at a poster that appears to read 'Kennedy Center DEMOLISHED'.

title: Former top civil servants: above all, make less policy

title: Paulien Cornelisse wears a cap in De slimste mens after chemotherapy: 'I absolutely did not want a wig'

title: René Froger calls off solo show: 'Very sensitive'
lead: René Froger (65) speaks openly on camera for the first time about his autoimmune disease, which forces him to take rest for the time being. In a personal video on Instagram he shares what the disease does to him and says he is losing more and more of his strength. That is why René is now focusing mainly on what matters most to him: his family.

title: Lionel Richie suffers from heart rhythm disorder and undergoes treatment: 'He hopes to resume work soon'
lead: No 'Dancing on the Ceiling' for Lionel Richie for a while: the 77-year-old singer has to take a step back for now after a procedure on his heart. So bad news for his fans, because as a result his next three concerts with 'Earth, Wind & Fire' have been called off.

title: Barred journalists allowed back into White House hours after refusal

lead: The Netherlands is returning to the Eurovision Song Contest after a year's absence. lead: For Ilse DeLange (49) her day is truly 'So Incredible', because after 18 years she is back in the Top40 with her monster hit, at number 16. Ilse says she finds it 'bizarre' and Mr Top40 Domien Verschuuren (38) explains how spectacular this is.

title: Luxury clothing brands are losing their shine: why customers are dropping out
lead: Catwalks, extremely expensive clothing, seeing and being seen: these are the images we know from a Fashion Week, such as the one now in Milan. But behind that glitter and glamour, luxury is losing its shine.

title: Netherlands going to the song contest after all, NPO handles entry
lead: The die is cast: the Netherlands will take part in the upcoming edition of the Eurovision Song Contest after all. After AVROTROS withdrew, participation still seemed uncertain. It will be a joint project of the public broadcasters.

lead: The Netherlands faces a wave of AI cyber attacks, say the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and intelligence service <entity id="org:directoraat-generaal-algemene-inlichtingen-en-veiligheidsdienst">AIVD</entity>, among others. Attacks are moreover becoming larger and more complex.

title: Suspect in fatal accident in Vogelwaarde may await verdict in freedom: why is that allowed?
lead: The suspect in the fatal accident in Vogelwaarde, in which three schoolchildren and their school head died, no longer has to await the criminal case from prison. The court has suspended his pre-trial detention under conditions. For the surviving relatives that feels like a blow. Yet this is exactly how Dutch criminal procedure works, two experts explain.

title: How much may migraine cost society? 'The disease mainly affects people in the most productive phase of their lives'
lead: Migraine costs Dutch society billions of euros annually. The largest part of that bill arises in the workplace. Yet we often continue to see migraine as a whiny little ailment.

Over the past ten years he already made his family business more sustainable with a lot of solar panels and thermal energy storage, an energy- and cost-saving method for heating and cooling buildings. The farm no longer uses gas, but still has a lot of electricity left over. With the electrolyser, farmer Karsten can still use his surplus electricity on sunny days…

title: Fifth person with West Nile virus has died, number of infections has risen
lead: Another patient who was infected with West Nile virus has died. The Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu ( <entity id="org:rijksinstituut-voor-volksgezondheid-en-milieu">RIVM</entity> ) reports this. Whether the virus was the cause of death, or for example fragile health, is not clear. This year, five people who were infected with West Nile virus have died. In the past week, the RIVM received sixteen reports of people in whom the virus was detected. That brings the number of people in the Netherlands who have been infected with the virus to 44. "All new patients got West Nile virus from the bite of an infected mosquito", the RIVM writes. In addition, 48 new infections were reported in horses and 71 in birds. Hospital admissions In most people, the virus was detected when they were admitted to hospital with symptoms. Most infections were in <entity id="org:provincie-zuid-holland">Zuid-Holland</entity>: 23 in total. This is followed by the <entity id="org:provincie-utrecht">provincie Utrecht</entity> with ten confirmed infections. People have also contracted the virus in <entity id="org:provincie-noord-holland">Noord-Holland</entity> (4), <entity id="org:provincie-noord-brabant">Noord-Brabant</entity> (4), <entity id="org:provincie-gelderland">Gelderland</entity> (2) and <entity id="org:provincie-overijssel">Overijssel</entity> (1). The RIVM estimates that the number of infections is in reality much higher. What is West Nile virus? You can read that and the answer to four other questions in this piece: People cannot infect each other with West Nile virus, except via blood transfusions or organ transplants. In one of the infected patients, the virus was found during a scientific study by blood bank Sanquin Research. Last week it emerged that the blood bank is now testing all blood donations in nine provinces for West Nile virus. That check had been abolished because the virus had not been found for years.

title: Room for new war victims too: Nationaal Ereveld Loenen expanded
lead: The Nationaal Ereveld Loenen is being expanded. The cemetery where Dutch war victims are buried thereby also gets room for those killed in future conflicts. There will be room for 1000 extra war graves, in addition to the almost 4000 current graves. The expansion was inaugurated with a ceremony. Several members of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> as well as surviving relatives were present. The expansion creates room not only for victims of future conflicts, but also for the fallen whose families can no longer care for the graves. During the ceremony, two war victims were reburied. Both were killed in Dutch service. The grave rights have therefore been transferred to the Oorlogsgravenstichting. Forever The Ereveld Loenen has been in use since 1949. Soldiers lie there, but also resistance fighters, political prisoners and Engelandvaarders. There is also room for victims of forced labour by Nazi Germany. Well-known names include that of the Surinamese anti-colonial writer and resistance hero Anton de Kom, who died in a German concentration camp. The grave of Ernst Cahn can also be found in Loenen. In 1941 he was the first resistance fighter to be executed by the Nazis. At the very end of the Second World War, Anda Kerkhoven was killed by the Nazis. As a student in Groningen she had taken part in the resistance. A month before the liberation of the city of <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity>, she was executed by the Sicherheitsdienst. She too is buried in Loenen. Nationaal Ereveld Loenen is managed by the Oorlogsgravenstichting; that foundation cares for some 50,000 war graves worldwide. Correction by the editors An earlier version of this article wrongly stated that resistance hero Willem Arondéus, one of the leaders of the attack on the Amsterdam population register in 1943, is buried in Loenen. 'Banker of the resistance' Walraven van Hall is also not buried at the Nationaal Ereveld Loenen. This has been corrected in the article.

title: White House admits journalists again after refusal, no live footage of Xi-Trump
lead: Reporters from Politico, CNN and MS NOW were denied access to the White House today. They were not allowed in, despite a court ruling. That ruling determined that journalists from Politico, CNN and MS NOW must be readmitted to the White House. Shortly after 18.00 (Dutch time), the barred media companies reported that they had been given access to the White House after all, well after the meeting there between the Chinese president Xi and his counterpart Trump. Boycott by Trump The press pass of the Politico reporter was confiscated by the Secret Service earlier today on arrival at the White House. He was then denied access to the grounds, writes Politico. CNN reporter Betsy Klein and a photojournalist were also denied access after several attempts. No reason was given for the refusal. Other CNN staff were allowed in. "CNN will keep trying to gain access", the media company said. The American president Trump announced this month that he would deny the three media companies access to the White House. Trump accused the three media companies of spreading fake news, but gave no concrete examples of this. No footage of Xi The refusal of the journalists came as the White House was preparing for the state visit of the Chinese leader Xi. It is a long-awaited meeting with events on the White House grounds, which are largely accessible to the press. The press conference of the two leaders was only accessible to a smaller group of White House reporters, also called the 'press pool'. Because the reporters and camera crews of Politico, CNN and MS NOW continued to be refused, other TV channels such as Fox News also decided not to take part in the pool, the group of major channels that usually take turns broadcasting the footage of press conferences and other important moments in the White House. The only footage of the meeting between Xi and Trump came from a signal that <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity>-Trump itself broadcast on the White House website. After the meeting between Xi and Trump, the barred media companies said they had access to the White House again. <entity id="org:rwt-nederlandse-omroep-stichting-nos">NOS</entity> correspondent Sjoerd den Daas explained in the NOS livestream why there is no footage of the meeting: The barring of the journalists led to considerable uproar and fierce criticism. American news media expressed their solidarity and broadcast a press conference with the American president without sound. CNN, MS Now and Politico went to court to have the decision reversed, invoking press freedom. The court withdrew Trump's measure this week for a period of fourteen days. Gulf of Mexico The cancellation of the press accreditation of CNN, MS NOW and Politico was a new chapter in Trump's long-running battle against media that, in his eyes, are not well disposed towards him. For example, since last year he has barred journalists from Associated Press because the American news agency did not adopt Trump's name change for the Gulf of Mexico (Gulf of America). He also regularly attacks journalists personally, especially women .

title: Fire at Starlink installation in Poland, deputy prime minister points to Russia
lead: The Polish authorities suspect that the fire that broke out yesterday evening at a Starlink installation was caused deliberately. According to deputy prime minister Gawkowski, there are several indications that a deliberate attempt was made to disrupt the operation of the Starlink installation. Exactly what those indications are has not been disclosed. Gawkowski suspects that Russia is behind the fire. That has not been established, but "much suggests that this fire fits in with the new Russian attack doctrine". The Starlink installation mainly supplies Ukraine with satellite internet. The network is used, among other things, for the operational communication of the Ukrainian army and also plays an important role in controlling drones. It is unclear to what extent the fire disrupted the internet connection. According to Gawkowski, the installation is simply operational today. According to European intelligence services, Russia reportedly wants to test NATO within a few months by carrying out small, possibly hybrid attacks on NATO territory. According to Gawkowski, this attack on the Starlink installation could be part of that strategy. The fire at the Starlink installation follows a series of other incidents in Poland. Earlier this month, a Ukrainian train on its way from Kyiv to Warsaw was attacked by a Russian drone. This week a Russian helicopter briefly entered Polish airspace.

title: From 'vaguely sweet' to 'window shut': Bietenradar predicts beet smell
lead: It is September, and that means beets are being taken from the fields again. They can bring quite a smell with them. Some find it smells pleasantly sweet, others find it sickly and sour. Anyone who does not want to be caught by surprise by the smell can consult the Bietenradar during the coming harvest weeks. An AI model uses weather information such as wind force and wind direction to calculate where the smell of sugar beet can be smelled, maker Maarten Oostland tells RTV Noord . He remembers listening last year to a sugar producer who talked about beet smell. "He explained that it was down to 'north wind, low-hanging clouds and sometimes some fog'", says Oostland. "I thought, that is just a weather forecast." Window shut The website shows the intensity of the smell, ranging from 'vaguely sweet' to 'window shut'. It also indicates where the smell is strongest at that moment. Initially, the site was only made for the area around the beet factory in <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity>. But right away many questions also came from people from the area around Dinteloord, in Brabant, where the other sugar beet factory is located, writes Omroep Brabant . "Whether we wanted to make a radar for that place too. That was done in no time." Besides weather information, the AI model also uses reports from users. These are shown on the map as dots. "The reports are processed to improve the AI model." The dots do not necessarily have to be next to a factory, because trucks with beets will be driving back and forth in the coming weeks to take the harvest from the fields to the sugar factory. The beet transport continues 7 days a week, 24 hours a day. Record yield In the Netherlands, some 85,000 hectares of sugar beet are grown every year. They are processed during the beet campaign. This year that campaign runs until January, and so it stops earlier than in other years. It also started later than normal; because of the dry summer, the beet yield turned out somewhat lower. "Now the beets have had an extra week to grow and produce sugar", farmer Remko van Wieringen said about this this week . That the campaign also stops two weeks earlier, in turn, has to do with last year's yield. It was so good that there is still a stock available.

title: Popular 'squishy dumplings' not dangerous, says regulator
lead: Squishy dumplings are not dangerous to health. The Nederlandse Voedsel- en Warenautoriteit (<entity id="org:nederlandse-voedsel-en-warenautoriteit">NVWA</entity>) investigated the hugely popular toy and found no health risks. Last summer, some shops withdrew the squeezable dumplings from sale after research showed that potentially harmful substances could be released. The NVWA also received complaints about the chemical smell of some products. According to the regulator, that smell can be released by the evaporation of so-called volatile organic compounds. These are also found in paint and turpentine , for example. In the laboratory, those substances were found in small amounts. So small that they pose no danger to health. Should people be concerned about the volatile substances, the NVWA advises them to let the toy air out in a well-ventilated room. The substances evaporate in a short time, the regulator says.

title: Radboud Universiteit bars far-right student association after NCTV and AIVD report
lead: The Groot-Nederlandse Studentenvereniging (GNSV) has been designated as right-wing extremist by the counterterrorism coordinator NCTV and the intelligence service AIVD. For the Radboud Universiteit in <entity id="org:gemeente-nijmegen">Nijmegen</entity>, that is reason to no longer admit the association to the next introduction fair for new students. The analysis by the intelligence service and the counterterrorism coordinator came out this week. In it, the AIVD and NCTV write that right-wing extremists are working to normalise their ideas online, via politics, the media and at demonstrations, and are becoming increasingly skilful at it. By far-right ideology, the AIVD and NCTV mean thinking in which white superiority is central, as is hatred of people with a migration background and people who think differently. 'Deeply racist' According to the report, the association presents itself as national-conservative, but behind the scenes members hold more extreme views. "For example, they see Flemings and Dutch people as one people, but then as one 'white' people", write the AIVD and NCTV. "Several (core) members of GNSV also express deeply racist views about Dutch identity." The student association is in favour of 'remigration' of Dutch and Flemish people with a non-Western background, it further states. That word has a meaning that is more extreme than is often admitted by the person using it, say the AIVD and NCTV. Clear and serious "Within the association, people are aware of the importance of presenting the ideology as acceptably as possible in order to come across as moderate", the analysis says. According to the AIVD and NCTV, this gives the association room on university campuses to recruit members and organise activities. "Membership of this group has thereby been normalised, while the underlying ideology and ideological ambitions are in reality right-wing extremist." And so the Radboud is taking measures. "The AIVD report is clear and serious", a spokesperson tells Omroep <entity id="org:provincie-gelderland">Gelderland</entity> . "It is important that the AIVD has designated the GNSV as a far-right organisation. That creates clarity and offers the university well-founded options to take measures." Geuzenbond GNSV was founded in 2021 in <entity id="org:gemeente-leiden">Leiden</entity>, by members of the Geuzenbond. On the anniversary of the death of the far-right politician Hans Janmaat, some members laid flowers on his grave. Janmaat was convicted in 1995, among other things, of discrimination and incitement to xenophobia. Last summer, a member of the association was arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist offence. He was acquitted of that, but he did receive a prison sentence of two years (one of which suspended) for illegal possession of weapons . Squabbling at intro fair The Nijmegen branch has existed since 2023. Since then, the introduction fair of the Radboud Universiteit has been a recurring topic of discussion every year. In 2023 a fight broke out at the GNSV stand - demonstrators did not agree that the association was allowed to recruit members among prospective students. Three people were arrested. The year after, the association again had a stand at the fair, but was given security. In 2025, GNSV withdrew from the fair, by its own account because of threats "from the far left". This year the students were initially welcome at the fair, but at the last moment the Radboud decided otherwise after all. According to the university, the safety of the members and visitors of the fair could not be guaranteed because of an announced demonstration at the stand. Besides Leiden and Nijmegen, GNSV has also had a branch in <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity> since January this year. There they were not at the introduction fair last summer; in Leiden they were. Utrecht University says that the association has never sought contact. The university therefore does not recognise or support the association. GNSV did not register for the previous introduction fair. Leiden University says it cannot yet say anything about possible measures against the presence of the association at the introduction fair.

title: Election of replacement for outgoing UN chief Guterres is proceeding with difficulty
lead: No white smoke, but leaked results. Behind closed doors in New York, a successor is being sought for UN chief António Guterres, who steps down on 1 January 2027 after two terms. This time something is missing that was always there early on in previous elections: a clear favourite. Officially, the 193 UN members appoint the new secretary-general. Heads of government and ministers from those countries are in New York this week for the annual summit, and there is busy speculation in the corridors. The choice is prepared in advance in the Security Council. There have now been three rounds of voting there, in which members can choose between approval, disapproval or no opinion. The secret voting rounds resemble a papal conclave, with the difference that the results almost always leak. But because voting is anonymous, the voting behaviour of the individual members remains shrouded in mist. Grynspan vs. Rodrigues-Birkett Former UN staff member Daniel Safran-Hon was the first to know the result of the first round. He is now an adviser to the International Peace Institute, a think tank. "The race is more exciting than ever", he believes. Former UN trade chief Rebecca Grynspan from Costa Rica narrowly received the most votes in the first round. Guterres and his predecessors Ban Ki-moon and Kofi Annan were already the favourite in the first voting round and eventually won as well. But this time the cards are far from dealt. On Friday, in a third vote, Grynspan received just the required minimum of nine votes. In the second round she had been overtaken by Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett, the UN ambassador of Guyana, who is now following her closely with eight votes. The Argentine Rafael Grossi also initially made a strong impression, but with five votes for and eight against appears to be out of the running. Russia also openly disapproved of the head of the UN atomic agency. And Michelle Bachelet, the first female president of Chile and former UN human rights commissioner, has herself already withdrawn from the race. Seven candidates remain. Wikipedia edited It appears that candidates have had their Wikipedia pages polished. UN watchers at PassBlue discovered that the Ecuadorian former president of the UN General Assembly was strikingly praised in a new passage. Blemishes, on the other hand, were polished away: for a former president of Senegal, "undemocratic manoeuvres", "repression" and a "coup attempt" were described in milder words. The front-runner mainly faced attacks. On Grynspan's page, a 'controversies' heading was added and removed again seventeen times within two weeks. New Wikipedia users tried to get a poorly substantiated rumour into her biography, but moderators intervened. Preferably a woman, from Latin America The two front-runners both come from Latin America. It is unofficially that continent's turn, although African candidates are also still in the race. According to Safran-Hon, Latin American countries must quickly unite behind one candidate. "Their unofficial turn is not set in stone." If the uncertainty continues, new candidates will come forward. In addition, there is a loud call for a woman. China would "like to see a woman", for the United Kingdom it is a priority and the non-permanent members of the Security Council are also pressing for it. Their vote carries the same weight as that of the permanent members, although they have no veto. According to minister Berendsen, also at the UN summit, it would be "very nice" if a woman wins. "Quality comes first, but there are plenty of women with the qualities to be a good secretary-general." Glass ceiling In 80 years, the UN has never been led by a woman. "How can we lecture companies about glass ceilings and keep them in place ourselves?", Sarah Hendriks wonders. The Canadian with Dutch roots is policy director of the UN women's organisation. "This election is a litmus test of whether this institution, which has always fought for gender equality, matches its words with deeds." The political emancipation of women is stagnating. In 54 UN member states, the number of women in parliament has even fallen, according to research by the UN and the World Economic Forum. The number of women in governments also decreased in two years. "At the current pace, it will take 171 years to achieve gender equality", Hendriks calculates. According to her, female leadership has substantial advantages. "When women are at the top, peace and economic prosperity follow. The data shows that." Coloured ballots If the election drags on too long, the monthly rotating president of the Security Council - now France, next month Greece - can decide to give the permanent members coloured ballots. It then becomes clear which candidates they support or reject, and candidates can draw their conclusions. According to Safran-Hon, one thing is certain: "It is the first time that at this stage there is still no convincing front-runner."

title: Podcast De Dag: Trump and Xi, friend and foe
lead: For the first time in eleven years, Chinese President Xi is back in Washington. In 2015 he last met then President Obama at the White House. And now he is there again with American President Trump for a state banquet and to talk about AI, trade and Taiwan. Listen here: You can listen to this episode of De Dag via <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister and all other podcast apps. Do you like it? Then don't forget to subscribe. And at De Dag we would like to know what you think of our podcast. When, and above all why, do you listen, and what could be better? Fill in the questionnaire here. Much appreciated! Correspondent Sjoerd den Daas caught Trump when he landed with his helicopter after picking up Xi. He sees an American president who wants to make Xi feel entirely at home. So he picks him up at the airport and calls him a good friend. But how strong is that 'friendship'? How does China view the US? From the way they try to profit from each other, a hostile picture also emerges. Who is the stronger of the two? Want to respond? Email dedag@nos.nl Presentation & editing: Marco Geijtenbeek Editors: IJsbrand Terpstra

title: Tweede Kamer wants broader and clearer ban on camera glasses
lead: The Tweede Kamer wants a clearer ban on camera glasses, and that ban must apply in even more situations than is already the case. "The pace cannot be fast enough", says Pro MP Kathmann. "The Netherlands is fed up. The unrest is incredibly great." The digital civil rights organisation Bits of Freedom and the Consumentenbond also want a ban on the 'peeping glasses' with a built-in microphone and AI. Many people are filmed in intimate situations without realising it. Those images are shared on social media. According to <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>, a ban is in principle not legally necessary because various legal rules already apply to the use of camera glasses and the video footage. The glasses may only be used privately, says state secretary Van Bruggen. "But I do understand the call from the Kamer." Punishable Making and sharing images of someone is not simply allowed. The right to privacy is laid down in the constitution, the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union and the European Convention on Human Rights. In addition, national and European consumer law applies to damage caused by products. And if someone suffers damage from being filmed without permission, this may constitute a tort. There are also portrait rights, the Copyright Act and the Criminal Code. Secretly filming in, for example, changing rooms and toilets is a criminal offence. Education, healthcare, hospitality, shops, gyms and swimming pools can already include an enforceable ban in their house rules. Actually already banned Kathmann acknowledges that the camera glasses are "actually already banned". But if so many people break the rules and so many people are bothered by it, then it must be "included more explicitly in guidelines", she believes. The CDA previously asked for a ban on camera glasses. The cabinet is awaiting advice this autumn from the European Data Protection Board on camera glasses, AI glasses and other "AI wearables" with built-in technology. The <entity id="org:zbo-autoriteit-persoonsgegevens">Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens</entity> (AP) is also represented on it. The AP is the privacy regulator in the Netherlands. On Tuesday, the AP expressly warned that in many situations the use of the glasses and the footage made with them is prohibited. Frightening Programme maker Roel Maalderink and the digital civil rights organisation Bits of Freedom criticise the camera glasses of Meta in a satirical video. Maalderink used the glasses to film Meta employees at the company's office in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>. The tech company removed the video from Instagram, part of Meta. "Frightening", says Kathmann. "This smacks of censorship." Meta says the video was removed because of alleged bullying and harassment. The video can still be seen on YouTube, part of tech giant Google. Google and Apple also want to bring AI glasses with a built-in camera to market. Incidentally, there are also applications of AI glasses that receive more positive reactions. For blind and visually impaired people, the AI function can help with reading texts aloud or finding locations. Doctors can let colleagues watch remotely during the treatment of a patient. There must be an exception to the ban for these applications, says the Tweede Kamer.

title: Germany investigates former camp guard (105) for murders in WWII
lead: In the German city of Dortmund, the public prosecutor has opened an investigation into a man of 105 who was a guard at a prisoner-of-war camp during the Second World War. The man is suspected of having murdered prisoners, and of having helped others commit murder. He was between 20 and 24 years old at the time. The state of health of the 105-year-old suspect is not known. He is not yet in custody. The man was stationed at the Stalag VI-K Senne camp, also known as Stalag 326. In that camp near the town of Schloss Holte-Stukenbrock, in the state of North Rhine-Westphalia, hundreds of thousands of captured soldiers were held between 1941 and 1945, mainly from the Soviet Union. When the camp was liberated by the Americans in April 1945, between 180,000 and 200,000 people were being held there. Prisoners in the camp were usually forced to work in nearby factories or mines. How many people died as a result of forced labour or violence by guards is not known, but it is estimated to have been many thousands of people. In recent years, very elderly former Nazis have more often been brought to court. In 2022, a 97-year-old man in Itzehoe was given a two-year suspended prison sentence for committing, or being complicit in, more than 10,000 murders. Demjanjuk In 2011, the former camp commander John Demjanjuk (then 91) was sentenced to five years in prison for the murder of more than 28,000 people in the Sobibor extermination camp, in Poland. He appealed and died in 2012 in a care home. That verdict set a new precedent: judges ruled that anyone who had ever worked in a Nazi camp was guilty of murder (and complicity in it) of the prisoners in the camp. Since then, prosecutors no longer have to prove that the suspects were actually personally involved in murders in a camp.

title: Spanish police stumble upon torture chamber and rescue two men
lead: Earlier this month, the Spanish police were able to rescue two people who had been tortured in a kind of torture chamber. The room was completely wrapped in plastic construction sheeting. There were pliers, hammers and other tools. But there was no renovation going on. The officers had come to the villa in Estepona in southern Spain because of a panicked phone call from the girlfriend of a man who had an appointment at the house. Because she had not heard from him, she raised the alarm. Officers went to the house and rang the bell, but nobody opened the door. To investigate the situation further, the officers climbed over a fence. At that moment a naked man, covered in blood, came running out, screaming: "They want to kill us." Tied up The horror was not over yet. In the house the officers found a man tied to a chair in a room that had been prepared in this way. At about the same time, two other men ran out of the house. A major alarm was then raised, because an arsenal of heavy weapons, including Kalashnikovs, was also found in the house. All available officers from the area were called in to guard the house. Meanwhile, the two men who had fled were tracked down. In the end, the police arrested seven men, all from Serbia. According to the police, they are members of an Eastern European criminal organisation. The two victims were presumably targeted because of a dispute over a shipment of drugs. Leaving no traces The police believe the perpetrators used the plastic to try to leave no traces in the house. That way, no blood or other biological material from either the victims or the perpetrators would remain on the floors and walls. The plastic would probably be burned once the torturing was over. The discovery was made at the beginning of September, but was made public this week by the outlet El Español . How long the torture chamber had been in use and whether the two men are the only victims has not been disclosed. The Spanish police have asked Interpol for help with the investigation and do not rule out further arrests.

title: Flattery back and forth at Xi's visit to Trump in the White House
lead: Chinese president Xi has been received by president Trump at the White House in Washington. In speeches the presidents showered each other with compliments, but they also made clear which political points of discussion are on the table during Xi's state visit. Xi said, among other things, that he is glad to visit "your beautiful country" and that he is in the US "to continue our friendship and expand cooperation". Trump said that he and Xi have "a great friendship" based on "mutual respect". Xi is in the US for a day and a half in the year in which the country celebrates 250 years of the United States. Trump said that tomorrow they will go to the <entity id="org:nationaal-archief">Nationaal Archief</entity> to "look at some of the greatest treasures of our proud history, including the Declaration of Independence and the constitution". Xi touched on artificial intelligence (AI) in his speech. "We have both the capacity and the responsibility to develop AI and to ensure that the development of AI always remains under human control and serves the well-being of the people." Both China and the US are very keen to become leaders in applying AI. At the moment it is the American tech companies that are ahead, but China is also investing heavily in AI. Read more about the AI race between the US and China here: Xi also stressed the importance of cooperation between the two economic superpowers. He called for improving communication between China and the US and for not regarding competition as a matter of winning or losing. "It must be a race to catch up with each other, not a struggle in which one wins and one loses." At the start of his second term Trump unleashed a trade war by introducing import tariffs, including on products from China. Xi responded at the time with extra import taxes on American goods. Last year the two reached a trade truce, which has led to somewhat better relations. They agreed on lower import tariffs. Chinese export restrictions on critical rare earth metals were also put on ice. Today the American <entity id="pos:minister-van-financien">minister van Financiën</entity> Bessent announced that the trade truce, which was due to expire in a month and a half, is being extended by two months. Panda diplomacy Xi also announced that over the next five years 100,000 American young people may come to China to study. China is also sending two pandas to a zoo in Atlanta in the coming days. Zoo Atlanta had already announced earlier this year that two pandas would be coming. Giant pandas occur only in China and the country regularly uses them as a diplomatic tool. It is a way for Chinese rulers to strengthen ties. China rents the animals to a zoo for a certain amount per year. Not live on TV Press conferences in the White House are usually broadcast live by the major American news channels. That is not the case this time because of the White House's refusal to admit reporters from Politico, CNN and MS NOW, despite a court ruling. Video recordings of the speeches were shot and distributed by the White House itself. As a result there is now little footage of Xi's visit to Trump:

title: Spineless or logical? Mixed reactions to the Netherlands' return to the Eurovision Song Contest
lead: The news that the Netherlands is returning to the Eurovision Song Contest after a year's absence is causing mixed reactions. An independent team of experts is to take charge of selecting the entry on behalf of the <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity>. The <entity id="org:rwt-nederlandse-omroep-stichting-nos">NOS</entity> is responsible for the coverage, the previews and the commentary. Broadcaster AVROTROS has decided the Dutch entry since 2010, but withdrew for the past and the coming edition because of Israel's participation. As a result the event has "lost its neutral character", according to the broadcaster, which does not consider participation to fit its own values. The broadcaster is also not taking part in the selection committee this year. 'No backbone' That the NPO is now taking on this task is meeting fierce criticism online. "Spineless again", "just as strong a backbone as Ed Sheeran", "no backbone" and "you should distance yourself from a country that commits genocide, not seek connection with it" are some of the reactions that can be read on platforms. A citizens' movement has also started an online petition calling on the NPO to reverse the decision to take part in the song contest. Because "the violence in Gaza and on the West Bank simply continues in the meantime", the initiators write. The appeal has by now been signed more than 25,000 times. The chair of the NPO explained the decision yesterday: Felix Pot, assistant professor of social geography at the Rijksuniversiteit <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity>, researches the politics around the Song Contest. He understands the criticism of and the cynicism around the Dutch participation. "AVROTROS withdrew for political reasons. If another party then takes over the organisation, I understand that this sends a certain signal to the public." For example, that the NPO considers the tightened rules of the EBU, the organisation behind the Song Contest, and the measures to limit political influence sufficient, Pot outlines. For instance, a country that wins the song festival while it is involved in a military conflict no longer automatically has the right to organise the next edition. "That is of course aimed at Israel", said Pot. Broadcasters and artists are also no longer allowed to actively take part in or contribute to promotional campaigns. According to the EBU the stricter rules are needed to counter influence on the voting process. The measures follow criticism of the Israeli participant Noam Bettan, who last year called on social media in several languages for people to vote for Israel. "This has been a difficult decision for the NPO", says Gerrit-Jan Kooijman, song contest expert and presenter of the podcast Ding-a-Dong about the Song Contest. "Because AVROTROS took an explicitly ideological position. That makes it complicated for the NPO, because it looks as if it does not share those positions of one of its broadcasters." According to Kooijman the decision also shows what the role of the NPO within the broadcasting system is. "All broadcasters have their own colour. The NPO stands above that and recognises that those different colours have value. It shows: you can fundamentally disagree with each other on one point, but that does not mean we do not respect each other." Able to withstand criticism Kooijman thinks it is logical that the NPO is taking the selection upon itself. According to him the song contest is an important stage for Dutch artists and thus part of the cultural mission of the public broadcaster. He does think it will be a difficult task for the NPO to find an artist who can withstand the criticism and hectic atmosphere around the Song Contest. A lot is involved in the preparation, the performance itself and the support, also from the broadcaster. According to Kooijman, the NPO has to "reinvent the wheel" in a certain sense. In the end Kooijman is not too worried about the search for a candidate either. According to him there is a lot of expertise within the broadcasters. He expects the candidate to be someone who is self-assured and has experience with media appearances. "And who approaches the song contest the way Duncan Laurence said after his victory in 2019: 'Music first'." According to him it will also be an artist surrounded by an experienced team. "Normally you are already much further in the selection process in September, but there is still time. With Claude two years ago a strong candidate was also put forward in a short time. There is enough talent available." Next year the Dutch entry will take the stage in the Bulgarian city of Burgas at a song contest that has long ceased to be just a song festival, Kooijman also sees. "The song contest will always have to change with the times and deal with criticism. We live in turbulent times and the song contest is a reflection of that."

title: Atlantic hurricane season at its peak, but where are they?
lead: August and September; normally these are months in which things can get very stormy on the Atlantic Ocean. Hurricane Katrina left a trail of destruction through New Orleans in 2005. And in 1992 hurricane Andrew did so in Florida in this period. A few years ago it was our own kingdom's turn, when hurricane Irma led to a lot of damage and deaths on the Windward Islands. Sint-Maarten in particular was hit hard. Usually the hurricane season is at its most intense around this time, but this year it is quiet. Dead quiet. On average some seven hurricanes and fourteen storms rage on the Atlantic Ocean each year. This year the count has so far stopped at six storms and not a single hurricane. It is the first time in more than a century that not a single hurricane has been seen this late in the year. Strikingly, it all has to do with the weather phenomenon El Niño. "It is really very quiet. As a hurricane scientist I am a bit bored", jokes Nadia <entity id="org:gemeente-bloemendaal">Bloemendaal</entity>, scientist at the <entity id="org:koninklijk-nederlands-meteorologisch-instituut">KNMI</entity>. "But it is not a given that nothing at all will form", she says. "The season runs until 30 November. We remain on our guard." Record number of severe hurricanes The driving force behind the small number of storms and the absence of hurricanes is a very strong El Niño. This natural phenomenon slows the formation of hurricanes on the Atlantic Ocean. Above the Pacific Ocean exactly the opposite happens. On 3 September Copernicus satellites saw three hurricanes at the same time on the Pacific Ocean for the first time since 2015: The situation there is therefore very different this year. Off the coast of Mexico, tropical storm Polo grew unprecedentedly fast into a hurricane of the most severe category. After that it did weaken somewhat. Polo is already the third very severe hurricane this year, equalling the record for the Pacific Ocean. And here too the season has a while to go. El Niño not only leads to more hurricanes and storms. They also take different routes, so that they end up more often in South Korea and Japan. The latter country was hit only this week by hurricane Dujuan. Very strong El Niño During an El Niño, trade winds above the Pacific Ocean weaken. As a result, relatively warm water ends up off the coast of South America. This is a natural variation that happens every three to seven years. The current El Niño is exceptionally severe. The water is already at about record temperature, while El Niño is usually only at its strongest in December. Although El Niño happens in the Pacific Ocean, it has effects across the whole planet. And not only in the sea but also in the atmosphere all kinds of things happen because of El Niño, says hurricane expert Bloemendaal. For example, an area forms in the east of the Pacific Ocean where air rises easily. To form a storm, air must also rise. "In an area where the airflow already wants to go upward by itself, such a storm therefore gets an enormous push", says Bloemendaal. <entity id="org:rwt-nederlandse-omroep-stichting-nos">NOS</entity> op 3 made this explainer video about El Niño in 2024: Above the Atlantic Ocean exactly the opposite happens during an El Niño. There is a descending airflow that actually counteracts the formation of storms. There are also large differences in wind speed and direction between the surface and high in the atmosphere, in other words wind shear. Storms form more easily precisely when those differences are small. Now that is much more difficult, Bloemendaal explains: "The wind shear now ensures that anything that tries to form is immediately blown apart" Warm seawater El Niño is not the only change that influences the number of hurricanes. In 2023, for example, there was an El Niño and it still became an active year for hurricanes above the Atlantic Ocean. "That was against our expectations as hurricane scientists", says Bloemendaal. "But the seawater of the Atlantic Ocean was very warm then. That meant so much energy was available that forming hurricanes could break through the descending airflow." This year too the seawater of the Atlantic Ocean is relatively warm, but not yet as warm as in 2023. Should no hurricanes at all appear on the Atlantic Ocean this year, it would be the first time since the 1960s. That is when scientists began to monitor the earth with satellites. If you go even further back in time, there were years in which people observed no hurricanes on the Atlantic Ocean. But the measuring instruments were more limited then. There were no satellites, for example. So it cannot be ruled out that people at the time missed hurricanes on the open sea that did not come near land.

title: Opposition attacks Van Weel in fierce debate over unprocessed police reports
lead: Many opposition parties are critical of the conduct of minister Van Weel (Justice and Security) in the matter of the unprocessed reports made by citizens to the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. Parties such as Pro, Groep Markuszower, SP, Denk, BBB, PVV and SGP want certainty that Van Weel is giving the Tweede Kamer the correct information about the number of reports that are left on the shelf at the police. This emerged in the first part of the debate in the Tweede Kamer on the 10,000 reports that are not investigated by the police. The <entity id="org:algemene-rekenkamer">Algemene Rekenkamer</entity> reported in June that nothing was done with thousands of reports of serious crimes in 2024. The Tweede Kamer wanted to question him closely about this. Motion of no confidence "We do not want a minister who sweeps crime under the carpet", said MP Lammers of the Groep Markuszower. "Does the minister actually have a grip on the figures?", SP MP Dobbe wants to know. A number of parties see a pattern in Van Weel's conduct. "He presents a sharp, firm picture to the Tweede Kamer and later it turns out to be different", says Denk MP El Abassi. JA21 MP Coenradie does not rule out submitting a motion of no confidence. "Is the minister not himself part of the problem?" BBB MP Van der Plas thinks that the minister of Justice lacks leadership, and Forum voor Democratie is already convinced, before the minister's answer, that he misinformed the Tweede Kamer. 'Half facts' The Tweede Kamer is calling Van Weel to account after the president of the Rekenkamer <entity id="person:pieter-duisenberg">Pieter Duisenberg</entity> said in a radio broadcast on Tuesday that Van Weel had misled <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity>. "With half facts an outcome is played down", said Duisenberg. Since the beginning of the summer there has been a sharp disagreement between Van Weel (VVD) and the Algemene Rekenkamer about the kind of reports left on the shelf at the police. In June the independent institution that audits government spending concluded that in 2024 nothing was done with about 10,000 reports of serious crimes, such as violent crimes. The police are struggling with staff shortages and have too much on their plate to get to these reports, according to the Rekenkamer. The matter took a different turn when Van Weel said in his response that there was a "distorted picture". According to the minister, the police mainly left aside reports that contained no leads. With this Van Weel created the impression that he was downplaying the figures and the problems, something he himself emphatically denies. Duisenberg's radio interview last Tuesday made clear that the Rekenkamer and the minister still do not agree on it. Human suffering Several opposition parties think that the open squabbling over figures is harmful to victims. "Behind these figures lies great human suffering", says Pro MP Mutluer. According to her, victims of serious crimes get the feeling that nothing is being done with their reports. Later this evening Van Weel will answer the questions of MPs and will have to explain exactly how things stand. And then the Tweede Kamer must make clear whether it is satisfied with this. The coalition parties D66, VVD and CDA are backing their minister. VVD MP Martens-America says that the minister and the Rekenkamer use different calculation methods. "That is very ugly." The CDA regrets that Van Weel caused "noise" and thinks it is a pity that he could have prevented this by saying that the data the ministry has do not match the data the Rekenkamer uses. "He did not misinform the Kamer", says CDA MP Straatman. But this coalition has no majority. JA21 MP Coenradie says that her confidence in the minister is "already quite damaged". If a majority of opposition parties supports a motion of no confidence, the opposition can therefore send a minister away. But it has not come to that yet. Political reporter Marleen de Rooy: "With this minority cabinet the opposition parties together have more seats, and they are keen to emphasise that today. In the past, with a majority cabinet, you saw in situations like this that a minister was protected by the coalition partners. A small mistake, better next time, and move on. But it is not that easy now. Minister Van Weel will therefore have to act this evening as a minister of a minority cabinet, with reflection and acknowledgement that he responded wrongly. How he will do that will become clear later in the debate once he has had his turn. Before the debate he already acknowledged on camera that things had not gone entirely well. And perhaps the sting will be taken out this evening. Wake-up call All in all, you can also see this as a kind of renewed wake-up call for this coalition. The three coalition parties can see that things can easily slip out of their hands as a minority cabinet. Apart from this subject and minister Van Weel, it is now also clear that none of the opposition parties feels bound to this coalition. Nobody sees the need to step into the breach for this minority cabinet. And that remains a vulnerability, which minister Van Weel experienced this evening."

title: Children's author Sjoerd Kuyper received the Gouden Griffel shortly before his death
lead: Children's author Sjoerd Kuyper has won the Gouden Griffel 2026 for his book Maantje verhuist de zee. Kuyper died two days ago at the age of 74. He received the prize last week in the presence of his family. Kuyper's grandchildren then visited him with flowers and cake to tell him the news: The Gouden Griffel is a jury prize for the best-written children's book. The jury praises the "literary quality, humour, warmth, creativity and imagination" that come together in a story "that takes children completely seriously" and "touches head, heart and imagination". He himself said about it last week: "In principle it is a very cheerful book, you can laugh a lot at it, but it is about a serious subject." The story is about Maantje, who writes a story for her seriously ill grandmother to cheer her up one more time. When grandmother has died, Maantje makes up stories to become cheerful again herself. The Gouden Penseel 2026 for the most beautifully illustrated children's book goes to illustrator Karst-Janneke Rogaar. She receives the prize for her book Lucy en Donker. The book is about the girl Lucy and the creature under her bed called Donker. Rogaar not only did the illustrations but also wrote the story. She will be presented with the prize tomorrow at the Kinderboekenbal. The Gouden Griffel is awarded every year to the best-written children's book. Kuyper previously won the prize for the book Robin en God from 1996. In 2012 he received the Theo Thijssen prize for children's and youth literature for his whole oeuvre. The jury praised the way in which he as a writer found the right words in all genres. "Sjoerd Kuyper can tell difficult things, even grand things, in simple language that nestles in your head and keeps singing around like a song. A very beautiful song."

title: Israeli election committee wants to exclude Arab parties from parliamentary elections
lead: A majority of the Israeli election committee has voted to exclude Arab political parties from the upcoming elections. The elections for the Israeli parliament, the Knesset, are at the end of October. The supreme court can still reverse the decision; that has happened more often in the past. The election committee is made up mainly of members of <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> of prime minister Netanyahu. The committee voted to block the participation of the United Arab List and the joint list of the parties Hadash, Ta'al and Balad. Individual Arab members of parliament were also excluded. The proposal to stop the participation of the far-right party Jewish Power of party leader Ben-Gvir was rejected. The committee's proposals claimed, among other things, that the Arab parties support the armed struggle against Israel. Individual Arab members of parliament were said to distance themselves insufficiently from Palestinian organisations. The Israel-based human rights organisation Adalah, which stands up for the Arab minority in the country, disputes those accusations. Key role According to opinion polls, neither Netanyahu's coalition nor the opposition can count on an absolute majority in the elections on 27 October. The United Arab List could possibly play a decisive role in securing the 61 seats needed for a majority in parliament, although many opposition leaders say they do not want to work with the party. The United Arab List was previously part of the government that Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid formed in 2021. The Arab parties condemn the step by the election committee. The United Arab List calls the exclusion "politically motivated and unacceptable". The joint list says that the decision is "political, racist and anti-democratic" and points out that the Arab parties in Israel represent some 1.25 million voters. The expectation is that the supreme court will reverse the decision next week. That also happened in 2019 and 2022 with similar decisions.

title: Hundreds of Delft students protest against unsafe streets with a bike ride
lead: In Delft this evening several hundred students protested against unsafe streets with a cycling procession. The protest follows a number of high-profile cases in recent months in which women were assaulted and sexually assaulted near the Delftse Hout nature area. Several student organisations set up the action and chose a protest by bike because the victims were also cycling when they were attacked. The choice of Thursday is also deliberate: many students go out on Thursday evening and night. "That the incidents happened precisely while cycling affects us", says chair Juliaan Kramer-Coenen of the SVCR, the umbrella of Delft sports and cultural associations for students, to Omroep Delft. "Students in Delft cycle to the training, rehearsal or drinks of their association and back home again. That precisely this habit cannot be done safely makes us angry." According to the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, over 300 people took part in the protest. Pre-trial detention extended Ten days ago a 19-year-old man from Delft was arrested who is suspected of the assaults and sexual assaults in and around the city. According to the police he confessed to being the perpetrator shortly after his arrest, and the suspect's DNA matches the material found on the victims. Today the man was brought before the examining magistrate, who ruled that he will remain in pre-trial detention for the time being: at least for the next two weeks.

title: Drents Archief warns of AI ghost sources in family tree research
lead: The Drents Archief is warning people about the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in, for example, family tree research. The archive increasingly sees people doing research with the help of AI and then requesting documents from the archive that turn out not to exist, or finds that names of people have been made up. The research done with AI looks real, but as soon as archive records are requested, it becomes clear that sometimes little of it is correct, Ellen van der Velds of the Drents Archief tells RTV <entity id="org:provincie-drenthe">Drenthe</entity>. "It is in birth certificates, death certificates or marriage certificates. It is stated very firmly: 'this must be there' and then it is not there. Or it is under completely different inventory numbers in our repository." According to Van der Velds, painful errors sometimes arise in family tree research in particular. As an example she mentions the name Jan de Vries from Emmen. "If I search our database for that name I already find about fifty of them. If I then do not state when he was born, and who his parents and grandparents were, AI starts reasoning by itself which Jan de Vries I mean." Painful errors The Drents Archief is not the only archive struggling with AI. According to Van der Velds the whole sector suffers from it. "We also know from other archives that about 10 percent of the questions were sent with AI. Or that AI was at least used in a piece of research." That can be annoying for the Drents Archief as well as for researchers, says Van der Velds. "The people doing research get 'convincing' evidence, but there are still errors in their family tree. It is also very annoying for us because it costs us a lot of extra time." Volunteers at the archive sometimes spend hours or days on research that is based on AI. Research that then yields nothing. Coming home disappointed For volunteer Koos Fokkens it is by now a familiar problem. Today he again received an email that he found suspicious given its layout. It was a list with bold letters, which often points to AI. The information requested in the email also ended in a dead end. And when he recently researched a historical murder case in Zweeloo, he was also disappointed. "Then you spend ages on it because you have to leaf through all kinds of physical court reports to establish whether there was such a case." After four weeks, the report on which the story was based turned out not to exist in the Drents Archief. Aid Even so, Fokkens himself does not find it frustrating. "Because it is wonderful work to do. You go on a search and are in fact solving a puzzle." The volunteer says that AI does not only cause problems, it can also be an aid. "It can put you on the track of a line of research you had not thought of yourself", he says. "If you look at it with expertise and are critical of the information provided, it can also be useful." Artificial intelligence can help, for example, with old spellings of place names, deciphering handwriting or ordering research results. The Drents Archief therefore stresses that it is not against the use of AI. "But we do say: keep thinking carefully yourself and check the sources that AI gives carefully", says Van der Velds.

lead: Archaeologists in Norg (<entity id="org:provincie-drenthe">Drenthe</entity>) are searching for Neanderthal treasures. Because it is such a time-consuming job, they cannot do without volunteers.

title: Heerma: deal more firmly with those who threaten political office holders
lead: In a committee debate on strengthening decentralised government, with the VVD notably absent, <entity id="org:ministerie-van-binnenlandse-zaken-en-koninkrijksrelaties">BZK</entity> minister <entity id="person:pieter-heerma">Pieter Heerma</entity> addressed, among other things, the democratic deficit in extended decentralised government and tackling threats and intimidation of decentralised administrators. 'All political office holders must be able to exercise political office safely and without forms of improper pressure.'

title: Power bank that caught fire on plane belongs to former KLM chief Camiel Eurlings
lead: The power bank that caught fire on board a KLM plane yesterday belongs to former KLM president and CEO Camiel Eurlings. Several sources on board the aircraft and with knowledge of the incident confirm this to RTL Nieuws. Eurlings reportedly suffered minor injuries in the incident.

title: Klopp: the Netherlands ideal opponent for debut with Germany
lead: For Jürgen Klopp, the Netherlands is the ideal opponent for his debut as national coach of the German national team. The 59-year-old coach said this on Wednesday during a press conference ahead of Thursday's Nations League match.

title: Eddy Zoëy pulls out all the stops for musical debut: 'Look at that handsome guy'
lead: Eddy Zoëy (59) and Levi van Kempen (38) are ready 'to shake things up' in musical land with a modern version of Shakespeare's 'Romeo and Juliet'. The international hit musical premieres on 7 October in <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity> and rehearsals are in full swing.

title: Rob Goossens enjoyed ranting Angela de Jong over Televizier-Ring nomination for De Bondgenoten: 'By all means turn up your nose'
lead: This week in his column 'Rob Reageert', Rob Goossens (36) looks at the three programmes in the running for the Televizier-Ring. The nomination of 'De Bondgenoten', among others, was not met with enthusiasm by everyone. Angela de Jong (50) and Maurice Wijnen (56), for instance, criticised the selection, to Rob's surprise.

title: G4 sound the alarm over homelessness
lead: The mayors of the four big cities (G4) see the homelessness problem in their municipalities rapidly worsening. The number of homeless people is increasing 'dramatically fast', and with it the number of nuisance reports. Concrete plans must be made to solve these problems, <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-rotterdam">Rotterdam</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity> write in an open letter to <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>.

title: Painful for the EU and Ukraine: two Russian oligarchs removed from the sanctions list
F-16 crashes in Michigan, pilot manages to escape
lead: An F-16 crashed during an exercise in the American state of Michigan. The pilot managed to escape. He was taken to hospital, but is in a stable condition.

title: 'To that young woman on her e-bike who ignored the zebra crossing: how would you explain that you rode into a toddler?'
Give the safety triangle a firmer position
lead: In the safety triangle, mayors and the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> (OM), as competent authorities, make crucial choices in consultation with the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> about the deployment of the available police capacity. Unlike in the safety regions, however, the working method of the safety triangle has been developed too little in recent years. In a time of social unrest and uncertainty and limited police capacity...

title: Men thought they had a 'date' with a 15-year-old girl, but had to drive around for hours and withdraw cash: OM demands 4 years against brothers for extortion
Indian Summer is on the doorstep, though we know it by another name
lead: September is coming to an end, but for now there is little sign of low temperatures, wind and rain. With warm and sunny weather, Indian Summer seems to have begun. Though in the Netherlands we know this phenomenon by a completely different name.

title: Diana's brother stands by controversial statement about King Charles: 'Exact words'
lead: The book 'Swansong' by Charles Spencer (62), Diana's brother, does not come out until next Tuesday, but it is already causing quite a stir this week. Earlier this week Earl Spencer claimed that King Charles (77) reacted to the death of Princess Diana with the words 'we will forget her soon enough'. King Charles immediately hit back in a statement that it had not happened. But an interview with the Earl has been published in which he says that he is telling the truth, and not the king.

title: Verstappen: keeping Hadjar as teammate 'completely logical'
lead: Max Verstappen is very pleased with Red Bull's decision to keep Isack Hadjar. The Formula 1 team has already signed the Frenchman for next season. "It is a completely logical decision. Isack deserves that seat", Verstappen said on the Formula 1 website. "I think it is good for everyone. I get on fine with Isack and it is good for the continuity in the team", said the four-time world champion.

title: Leader of very young pickpockets in Paris sentenced to eight years in prison
lead: The 48-year-old leader of a gang of children who roamed Paris as pickpockets was sentenced on Wednesday to eight years in prison for human trafficking. According to the French <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, the children brought in an average of 25,000 euros a day.

title: Diana's brother defends statements about Charles in new book: 'Monstrous'
lead: Charles Spencer (62), the brother of Princess Diana, stands by the statements he makes about King Charles (77) in his new book. In an interview with the BBC, Spencer insists that in his book he is telling the truth about a phone call with Charles after his sister's death.

title: Jan van Halst hears from son Mick in Race Across The World what he always hoped for as a father
lead: Jan van Halst (57) is moved in 'Race Across the World' by an unexpected remark from his son Mick. During a long bus ride in Turkey the two talk about friendship and the people who are important to them. Mick's words make Jan proud and emotional.

title: Phil and Yvette discover after arrival that things have disappeared from lodge: 'Everything is gone'
lead: Phil and Yvette, together with their children Izy (17) and Yves (19), swap Limburg for South Africa. After their first night they are immediately confronted with the facts of the large income inequality in the country: almost everything turns out to have been taken. You can see 'Het Roer Om' every Monday at 21.27 on NET5.

title: VVD minister Van Weel (Justice) under fire in the Tweede Kamer
lead: The opposition is very critical of justice minister <entity id="person:david-van-weel">David van Weel</entity> on Thursday evening. The debate is extra tense because the coalition is in the minority.

title: Anouk comes with a musical surprise in Ziggo Dome: 'Let yourself be surprised'
lead: Anouk (51) is taking the Metropole Orkest with her next year to her performances in the Ziggo Dome in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>. The concerts take place on Friday evening 4 June and Sunday afternoon 6 June.

title: From Best Kept Secret to Paradiso: the Netherlands' most progressive band comes from Kapelle in Zeeland and is called Grote Geelstaart. 'Every song is about pride and the sea'
lead: With neurotic Dutch-language noise rock, the young guns of Grote Geelstaart from Zeeland are conquering stages at home and abroad. Although they rebel against village narrow-mindedness, their new EP Wij zinken is inextricably linked to their native soil. "That we can stand on this dike without being washed away is becoming less and less a given."

title: Mass shooting in South Africa: '11 victims rounded up and shot dead'
lead: A party in a residential area in South Africa has ended in a bloodbath. A house in a suburb of Durban was stormed by armed suspects last night. At least eleven people were shot dead.

title: Cabinet presents ambitious housing plan, but 100,000 homes remains a heavy task
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> is presenting an action plan today to tackle the housing shortage. It should lead to 100,000 new homes per year until 2035. Whether that target will be met remains to be seen. "The plans are there, now it comes down to implementation", housing minister Elanor Boekholt-O'Sullivan (D66) writes to the Tweede Kamer.

title: Panic on board: cargo ship rams fishermen near Singapore
lead: This footage shows a cargo ship colliding with a fishing boat in the waters near Singapore. The BBC has confirmed that the footage is real, but little is yet known about how the collision happened.

title: Overasselt suspects spill the beans in statements: 'Everyone had to die'
lead: Detectives are working overtime in the investigation into the fatal group attack in Overasselt at the beginning of this month. Clarity seems to be coming on the main question of who exactly did what. In statements that are as explosive as they are startling, several suspects have reportedly spilled the beans completely, De Telegraaf writes.

title: Irritated Van Dijk feels too little appreciation at Oranje
lead: Virgil van Dijk feels too little appreciation in the Netherlands team. The captain spoke out about it on Wednesday during a press conference, where he gave a somewhat irritated impression.

lead: If labour is structurally taxed more heavily than wealth, too much wealth and power automatically ends up with a small group, sees former state secretary Marnix van Rij . The Box 3 issue is an opportunity for Dutch politics to do something about that.

lead: Lansingerland previously took documents in the council information system (<entity id="org:rijksinkoopsamenwerking">RIS</entity>) offline after it emerged that personal data in them were unintentionally publicly accessible. title: Build a collective housing complex for older people too

lead: The largest LAN party in the Netherlands is taking place in <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity> this weekend: The Reality. It is the twentieth edition of the gaming festival.

lead: He slept in a wheelie bin, in his old shed, in doorways and sometimes simply not at all. Twenty years ago the life of bestselling author Lex Paleaux (48) looked very different. And yet also not. "On a shitty day I am in the Nike store paying for new sneakers and for a moment it feels as if life is smiling at me, but as soon as I open the box at home, the effect has worn off."

title: IKEA to come to the Netherlands next year with 'supermarket-sized' stores
lead: IKEA is expanding in the Netherlands by opening 'supermarket-sized' stores next year. The new stores will sell everyday items, such as lighting and tableware.

Bram Krikke causes hilarious confusion in De Staatsloterij Show
lead: Lizzy is given the task of describing as many well-known Dutch people as possible to Nils. When it is the turn of Bram Krikke (32), that turns out to be easier said than done. Lizzy's hints send Nils down a completely different track, so that he comes up with a surprising new name for Bram. 'De Staatsloterij Show' can be seen every Saturday at 20.00 on SBS6.

title: On extreme weather the Netherlands can learn a lot from countries in Africa, say WFF and Red Cross. 'In disasters you depend on each other'
lead: What can the Netherlands learn from Africa and Asia about the response after extreme weather? In South Limburg, which was hit by heavy rainfall and floods five years ago, the World Wildlife Fund and the Red Cross have joined forces for a project that brings experiences from other countries to the Netherlands.

lead: Famke Louise (27) celebrates her 10-year anniversary as an artist next year. The artist does so with a concert in AFAS Live in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>. It will be her biggest solo show so far, concert organiser MOJO announced on Monday.

title: 'Fucking gay': these pupils notice that LGBTI acceptance is declining
lead: The acceptance of homosexuality among pupils has decreased in recent years, research shows. Pupils tell how they notice this: from slurs in the schoolyard to moments when they feel unsafe.

title: Wibi Soerjadi cuts concert short due to technical defect: 'Sincerely sorry'
lead: Wibi Soerjadi (56) ended his performance at Concertzaal <entity id="org:gemeente-tilburg">Tilburg</entity> early. title: Two pedestrians seriously injured in collision with tram in Rotterdam
lead: In Rotterdam two pedestrians were seriously injured last night in a collision with a tram. It went wrong on the 2e Middellandstraat in the Delfshaven district.

title: Municipal operations under pressure
lead: Developing future-proof operations requires a multi-year approach. Municipalities can only continue to carry out their social tasks by investing structurally in capacity, quality and renewal and by keeping services to residents and businesses at the desired level.

title: Paul Haenen stops playing Bert from Sesamstraat after 50 years: 'A new generation is coming'
lead: Paul Haenen (80) is stopping after more than fifty years with dubbing the voice of Sesamstraat puppet Bert. The actor announced this in his TV programme 'Margreet Dolman Begrijpt 'T' on RTL 4. lead: It is precisely in journalism that you see the damage done by postmodernism, Joris van Os observes: even the pursuit of objectivity is made subordinate to personal experience.

title: What does it mean to be a mathematician? The arrival of AI forces us to think about that question
lead: Mathematics is the first scientific field to be hit amidships by artificial intelligence. But the essence of the discipline lies beyond the capabilities of AI.

Lenny Kravitz joins special line-up with his own Ken doll
lead: Barbie maker Mattel has developed a Ken doll that looks like Lenny Kravitz (62). The singer tells PEOPLE that he thinks it is 'so cool' to have his own doll.

title: Zidane feels more emotion at coaching debut than as a player in 1994
lead: IZMIT (ANP/AFP) - Zinédine Zidane feels more emotion around his debut as national coach of the French national team than at his debut as a player for 'Les Bleus' in 1994. The 54-year-old coach said this on Thursday in the run-up to France's Nations League match in and against Turkey on Friday.

title: Marius Borg Høiby does not ask permission to attend funeral of Princess Astrid
lead: Marius Borg Høiby (29) will not attend the funeral of the Norwegian Princess Astrid on Wednesday. The son of Queen Mette-Marit (53) did not ask permission to do so, the Norwegian newspaper Nettavisen reports.

title: Kamer wants an end to costly member recruitment by broadcasters to prevent 'waste of money'
lead: PRO and VVD want to prevent public broadcasters from again spending hundreds of thousands on member recruitment next year, while that obligation disappears in 2029. lead: The talents of status holders, asylum seekers and Ukrainian displaced persons are insufficiently used in the Netherlands. According to a new advisory report from the Sociaal-Economische Raad (SER), these newcomers should be helped into work better, for example in sectors with staff shortages.

lead: In Germany the far right emerged relatively late, but the movement manifests itself in the AfD in a very radical way, says political scientist Léonie de Jonge. However, Germany also still has a resilient society. "When the AfD wins somewhere, people elsewhere take to the streets."

lead: Kees Jan and Lynn did not find love during their adventure in 'B&B Vol Liefde', but after the reunion there turned out to be a special click between the two after all. They sought each other out more and more often, got on very well and are now even dating exclusively.

title: At least ten people arrested at 'grim' protest in Opheusden against possible asylum centre
lead: At least ten people were arrested last night at a demonstration in Opheusden in Gelderland. The protest took place at the town hall, where a meeting was being held about the possible reception of asylum seekers in the future. In the course of the evening the atmosphere turned grim.

lead: The Dutch tennis players are close to a place in the first round of next year's Qualifiers in the Davis Cup. Tallon Griekspoor beat Colombian Nicolás Mejía convincingly in two sets (6-2 6-4) in the Maaspoort in Den Bosch and gave captain Paul Haarhuis's team a 2-0 lead.

title: Storm off Mexico grows into hurricane of the heaviest category in no time
lead: Off the coast of Mexico a tropical storm grew into a category 5 hurricane, the highest category, in a single day. Meteorologists call the speed at which the hurricane gained strength 'very remarkable'. The storm will probably not make landfall, but it can cause flooding.

title: Growth fund makes a fresh start
lead: The Nationaal Groeifonds is back. According to the Miljoenennota, an amount of 375 million euros will be set aside annually between 2027 and 2031 for a new round of the Nationaal Groeifonds.

lead: Rower Marloes Oldenburg, Olympic champion in the coxless four at the 2024 Paris Games, is going to row again. She announced this on Instagram. The 38-year-old Oldenburg ended her elite sports career in March 2025.

lead: Robbert Rodenburg (28) did not tell the whole truth during a conversation on 'RENZE'. title: Astrid Holleeder 'in love with life' now that she has left anonymity: 'Want to inspire other women'
lead: Astrid Holleeder (60) stepped out of anonymity in September 2025. Since then her life has changed considerably: after years of hiding she can walk the streets freely again. Two deaths had previously been linked to the roller coaster.
