lead: 'Niemand Wil Een Popster' is high in the charts and is now also a big hit on TikTok. Isabèl Usher had not seen the enormous success of her song coming herself and is overjoyed.

title: People in Berlin react to gains by AfD and Die Linke
lead: Germany was known as a country of stability. It was often the same parties that called the shots, a chancellor often stayed for at least a decade and the economy ran as if by itself. But something has changed with the eastern neighbours. The radical-right Alternative für Deutschland is gaining more and more ground and yesterday won a state election for the second time. title: The Match , about the World Cup match of 'the hand of God', is an irresistible journey back in time
lead: The story of the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina has been told often in forty years. But rarely with as much love for detail as in the recently released documentary by two Argentine makers.

title: Cabinet tackles 'scheefwonen' harder with higher rents and asset test
lead: Getting a social rental home will become a lot harder for people with a lot of savings or a substantial investment portfolio. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> is introducing an asset test for this. Rents for tenants whose income is too high for their social rental home are also going up sharply.

title: Video about poor-quality products goes viral: 'My name is Death'
lead: "Everything around me dies." That is how a dark campaign film by the Norwegian consumer association that is currently going around the world begins. It is about manufacturers that make products that break ever faster and are ever harder to repair. "This is brilliant", the Dutch Consumentenbond responds.

title: Supervision of the supervisor
lead: I remember one time when I came to pick up my daughter. In the garden I saw children playing. The only supervisor present had his eyes glued to his phone, writes FD columnist Sanne Kloosterboer.

title: Jetten visits iconic gay bar in New York: 'I feel a personal responsibility'
lead: Prime minister Jetten is in New York for the UN summit and during this visit is also stopping by the well-known gay bar Stonewall Inn. The owner of the bar appreciates the prime minister for his commitment to the LGBTI community and has therefore given him a special gift.

title: Ben Saunders's loved ones in tears at public farewell: 'He will always remain a loving man'
lead: On Tuesday a shock went through the country when it became known that 'The voice of Holland' winner Ben Saunders had died. The singer's tragic death affects many. On Saturday, fans therefore gathered at his tattoo shop in <entity id="org:gemeente-arnhem">Arnhem</entity> to pay a final tribute.

title: Darter Nijman through to next round at World Series Finals
lead: Wessel Nijman has qualified for the second round of the World Series of Darts Finals. The 26-year-old from Noord-Holland beat 57-year-old Australian Simon Whitlock 6-4 in the AFAS Live in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>.

title: Gordon keeps faith in love: 'Will always keep believing in it'
lead: Friday is a festive day for Gordon (58). Not only is his new single 'Omdat ik zo van je hou' with Lisa-Rose (25) coming out, the singer is also making his debut as a BABS: Buitengewoon Ambtenaar van de Burgelijke Stand.

title: Robert van Hemert makes debut at Holland Zingt Hazes: 'Reason I started singing'
lead: The fans of André Hazes will surely become 'a little bit in love' with this. RTL Boulevard may announce that Mart Hoogkamer (28), Robert van Hemert (33) and Numidia (26) have been added to the line-up of 'Holland Zingt Hazes'. For Robert it is his debut. We spoke to Mart about this festival earlier. After all these years he remains grateful that he gets to do this.

title: Widower Ivo (74) receives €4,138 a month and thinks about what he'll leave behind: 'My daughters are already doing well'
Actor Samuel L. Jackson and wife receive award for their commitment
lead: Actor Samuel L. Jackson (77) and his wife LaTanya Richardson Jackson (76) are being honoured for their social commitment. The couple will receive the Clarence & Jacqueline Avant Humanitarian Award during the annual gala of the HollyRod Foundation, Variety reports.

title: Result long since settled, yet millions of Russians vote for Putin again
lead: From today Russians can go to the polls for parliamentary elections. As always, the party of President Vladimir Putin is the presumptive winner. Why does Putin even bother to still hold elections?

title: 'Monster' has been one of the most successful Netflix titles for a while, yet the content gets no further than: look, murderers
How do you survive an ultrarun?
'Suddenly I felt an intense pain in my head and fell to the ground'
Tjeerd Royaards
Van Weel eats humble pie over statements about Court of Audit report: 'I apologise for that'
lead: Justice minister <entity id="person:david-van-weel">David van Weel</entity> (VVD) has apologised for remarks he made about a Court of Audit report on serious crimes that the justice system did not pursue. With his 'nuance' he gave the impression that he was questioning or downplaying the report, and that was not the intention, he said in the debate on the matter.

title: Three weeks after the disaster, hope of survivors in the Nepalese mud has vanished
lead: More than three weeks after a churning torrent of water, mud and debris raced through Nepal, hope is evaporating that survivors will still be found in the disaster area, which is covered with a thick layer of silt. In the damaged homes, personal belongings left behind bear witness to the lives destroyed by the disaster.

title: 'Ongehoord Nederland disgusts me', right-wing parties also turn against the broadcaster
Frans Bauer constantly at grandson Jantje's door: 'Already been 8 times by 3 o'clock'
lead: Since the arrival of his first grandson, Frans Bauer (52) has gained a favourite destination. A new episode of 'De Bauers' shows that the singer would like nothing better than to drop in at Jantje's every day. One visit a day is nowhere near enough for the new grandfather.

title: Gouden Griffel for 'Maantje verhuist de zee' by writer Sjoerd Kuyper, who died on Tuesday
'Economist Jona van Loenen seems not to understand the most basic economic concepts'
ADE 2026: the best not yet sold-out parties during Amsterdam Dance Event
Foundation problem in Amsterdam probably bigger than thought: 'Going to collapse like a house of cards'
Tom Jones grateful for support after forced departure as The Voice UK judge
lead: Tom Jones (86) is grateful for all the messages and expressions of support after his 'forced' departure as a judge on 'The Voice UK'. Earlier this month the singer wrote that he had been sent away as a judge by broadcaster ITV and that he would get a much smaller role in the fifteenth season of the talent show, which is currently being recorded.

title: Queen Máxima and Queen Mathilde side by side at UN meeting
lead: Queen Máxima (55) and Queen Mathilde of Belgium (53) sat next to each other on Tuesday during the 81st General Assembly of the United Nations at the UN headquarters in New York. That can be seen in photos of the meeting.

title: British anti-migration activist arrested after puncturing dinghy on the Channel during livestream
lead: The British anti-migration activist Daniel Thomas has been arrested by the British <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> on suspicion of endangering a life. On the Channel, Thomas stabbed with a knife into a dinghy in which a French aid worker was still sitting at that moment. He showed that moment during a livestream.

title: Not a token appointment, but really making room
lead: Preferential appointments for people at a disadvantage can be good. But institutions often mainly want to look good with them, and the appointee is above all expected to be grateful.

title: Municipalities claim few building costs from property developers
lead: Municipalities by no means recover all public costs of area developments from the property developer. In doing so, they leave money on the table. And the number of municipalities that claim a high amount per home is falling. Municipalities would therefore do well to develop policy.

title: Asylum children exposed to unsafe living conditions
lead: Children in emergency asylum shelters are now structurally 'exposed to unsafe living conditions that pose serious risks to their development', writes the Onderzoeksraad voor Veiligheid (<entity id="org:zbo-onderzoeksraad-voor-veiligheid">OVV</entity>) in the report 'Kinderen in nood' published on Monday. The OVV therefore calls on the minister of Asiel en Migratie to improve the situation of these children in emergency asylum shelters within six months.

title: The evolution of laughter, and why humans are the biggest gigglers
Affordability of care under pressure: 'Abolish the municipal policy, arrange it nationally'
lead: Where you live determines how well you are protected against high healthcare costs. Some 160,000 people currently have no municipal policy because the municipality does not offer one or contributes too little to the premium, according to research by the independent think tank Instituut voor Publieke Economie (IPE). The IPE advises abolishing the municipal policy and arranging the protection of people in poverty against high healthcare costs nationally.

title: AI agent breaks into website of Australian healthcare system, prime minister calls it 'unacceptable'
lead: An AI agent from OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, broke into the website of the Australian healthcare system in June. Other Australian government websites may also have been affected. Australia was notified two weeks ago. The country's prime minister finds it disturbing and calls both the incident and the way it was handled 'unacceptable'.

title: OpenAI hacked with AI model from competitor Anthropic
lead: Using one AI model to hack another. That is how researchers at security company Hacktron managed to break into OpenAI, the company behind chatbot ChatGPT, within 72 hours. After reporting the vulnerabilities to Open AI, they received a reward of the equivalent of 5700 euros.

title: Man (82) dies after argument over sunbed on Greek beach
lead: An 82-year-old man has died after an argument over a sunbed on a beach in Greece, local media report. The situation was reportedly so chaotic that the shouting could be heard on the other side of the beach.

title: Children help out at father Jay Lopez's work in Een Huis Vol
lead: Taking a child along to work has by now become quite normal for the Lopez family. And by the looks of it they are not only pleasant company, but also quite handy. 'Een huis vol' can be seen weekly on Friday and Saturday at 19.00 on KRO-NCRV on <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> 1.

title: Hoe Zuid-Afrika kan voorkomen dat het een maffiastaat wordt
lead: Georganiseerde misdaad kan worden verslagen, als er de politieke wil voor is.

title: Marius Borg Høiby chooses new defence for appeal
lead: Marius Borg Høiby (29), the son of the Norwegian Queen Mette-Marit (53), will be defended by other lawyers during the hearing of his appeal. They are Alexander Greaker and Daniel Storrvik, Norwegian media reported on Thursday. The lawyer duo also says it will come with new evidence that was not dealt with during the trial.

title: Ruben kisses Bing in GTST, but is rudely pulled out of his daydream
lead: The kiss between Bing Mauricius (Everon Jackson Hooi, 44) and Ruben Prins (Diego Clark-González, 36) already caused surprised reactions when the first images of the new season of 'Goede Tijden, Slechte Tijden' appeared. On Tuesday evening it finally became clear how things stand. Ruben and Bing do indeed kiss, but reality turns out to be somewhat different.

title: Verstappen has Hadjar back as teammate at Azerbaijan GP
lead: Max Verstappen will have Isack Hadjar as his teammate at Red Bull again for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in Formula 1. The team announced this on social media. The Frenchman missed the last races in <entity id="org:gemeente-zandvoort">Zandvoort</entity>, Monza and Madrid due to a wrist injury.

title: Provinces also sign agreements on crop protection
lead: The provinces have also backed the agreements that state secretary <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">Silvio Erkens</entity> made two months ago with seven organisations on the use of plant protection products. The provinces were missing when a covenant was signed in July, although they were involved in drawing it up. According to a spokesperson for the Interprovinciaal Overleg (IPO), all provincial executives still had to take a decision on the agreements.

title: Flikken Rotterdam actress Ortál Vriend gives birth to first child: 'We are so in love'
lead: Ortál Vriend (34) and her partner Axel have become parents of their first child. The 'Flikken Rotterdam' actress announces the baby news on Instagram and immediately reveals the name of their son.

title: Cherry-Ann Person buys a 5000 euro children's bed, but daughter refuses to sleep in it
lead: A children's bed of around 5000 euros sounds like a place to drift off into lovely dreams. Not for the daughter of 'The Real Housewives of <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>' star Cherry-Ann Person (38). Jayla (3) finds her transparent bed 'terrifying' and refuses to sleep in it, her mother tells LINDA.

title: Almost €4 for a litre of diesel
lead: This week it emerged that the United States was reportedly considering an export ban on diesel. That would send the price at the pump soaring.

title: Dog of Norwegian Princess Astrid dies shortly after its owner
lead: The little dog of the recently deceased Norwegian Princess Astrid has died. Wilma, who was the princess's loyal companion for years, reached the age of 12 and died shortly after her owner.

title: Zeeland waarschuwt voor olievervuiling op stranden
lead: Op meerdere stranden in Zeeland is olie aangespoeld, en de provincie heeft gewaarschuwd dat zwemmers weg moeten blijven uit...

title: Putin seizes Nestlé assets; company wants to take steps
lead: President Putin has placed the Russian divisions of the Swiss food group Nestlé and the French supermarket Auchan under the temporary management of a Russian organisation. It is the largest seizure of foreign business activities in Russia in two years.

title: Actress Hayden Panettiere died from combination of drugs and medication
lead: Actress Hayden Panettiere died as a result of using the painkiller fentanyl and several other medications. The coroner in Greenville County in the American state of South Carolina established this, Deadline reports. Her death has been classified as an accident.

title: Ian inconsolable after letter from girlfriend in De Bondgenoten: 'Come home now'
lead: The alleged spark between Ian and Joshlyn has an emotional sequel in 'De Bondgenoten'. Ian receives a letter from his girlfriend that begins as a grand declaration of love, but ends with a crystal-clear message: she wants him to come home immediately.

title: Hyves returns after thirteen years: radio DJ Barry Paf becomes new face
lead: Hyves is back as a social network after thirteen years. Owner Mediahuis, known for newspapers such as De Telegraaf and De Limburger, thinks there is a need in the Netherlands for an alternative to Facebook that deliberately does not use addictive algorithms and endless scrolling. Radio DJ Barry Paf (47) becomes the face of profiles without a photo on the platform.

title: Security services warn of quiet rise of far-right ideas
lead: Right-wing extremists are trying to make their ideas acceptable to a larger group of people by presenting a 'softer version' of them. Some supporters of the far right are also trying to influence political parties from within.

title: Surprising departure of chief executive of razor company Boldking
lead: Chief executive Piet-Hein Smit of razor company Boldking is leaving. This while at the beginning of this year he was still named as a prospective shareholder. The company repeatedly claimed in recent years to be making a profit, but that turns out to be nonsense.

title: Known risk became reality: this is why the A28 at Nijkerk had to close in a hurry
lead: Early last week it happened again: once more <entity id="org:rijkswaterstaat">Rijkswaterstaat</entity> had to close a bridge in great haste. This time in the A28 motorway at Nijkerk. While the problem has been known for years. That it still went wrong is due to a combination of circumstances, a reconstruction by RTL Nieuws shows. "If it happens more often in the future, you do have to be more alert."

title: He was there, the 83-year-old conductor Daniel Barenboim. Frail, stumbling and trembling, but he was there
lead: In recent years it has been uncertain until the last moment whether Daniel Barenboim can still mount the podium. He is ill and frail. But on Tuesday evening he led 'his' special West-Eastern Divan Orchestra in the Concertgebouw in Amsterdam.

title: This documentary brings on tech thinkers for the question: is it wise to have children in the age of AI?
lead: In The AI Doc, Oscar-winning director Daniel Roher hopes to suppress his panic about the future of the world. He does not entirely succeed, but he asks the right questions of the right people (though there are a few too many of them).

title: Gordon wishes sick René Froger strength despite lack of contact: 'Seems terrible to me'
lead: The news about the health of René Froger (65) also affects Gordon (58). Although the former colleagues have not been in contact for some time, Gordon sympathises with him. He tells RTL Boulevard this.

title: Evenepoel first rider with four consecutive world time trial titles
lead: Remco Evenepoel has become the first cyclist ever to become world time trial champion for the fourth time in a row. The Belgian Olympic champion lived up to his role as favourite in Montreal, Canada, and convincingly beat two-time world champion Filippo Ganna. After 39 largely flat kilometres, the 30-year-old Italian lost almost a minute to his rival, four years his junior. The French revelation Paul Seixas finished third.

title: Unrest within family after death of Ben Saunders: 'Sad'
lead: Ben Saunders will be buried in private on Wednesday, but on Tuesday it became clear that not the whole family will be present.

title: Search for budget support may take a while yet, according to Heinen
lead: <entity id="pos:minister-van-financien">Minister van Financiën</entity> <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Eelco Heinen</entity> (VVD) still wants to seek broad support. "But the vote is not until the end of the year, until then we will keep working on majorities." He says this in the weekly conversation with the minister of Finance on RTL Z. The minister is optimistic and has "every confidence that it will turn out fine." <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> will soon invite opposition parties to sit down at the table again.

title: Norwegian royal couple in front row at funeral of Princess Astrid
lead: The Norwegian royal couple Haakon (53) and Mette-Marit (53), Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra (22) and Queen Sonja (89) took their seats in the front row at the funeral of Princess Astrid. Princess Märtha Louise (55), her three daughters and her husband Durek Verrett (51) are also present. The public funeral of the Norwegian princess is taking place in the Ris Kirke in Oslo.

title: Almost 16 years in prison and tbs demanded against Dennis van E. on appeal in Diemen 'abortion murder'
Politicians who keep calling for an age limit for social media are treating symptoms
lead: Commission President Ursula von der Leyen last week announced a minimum age limit for social media within the EU. This puts fundamental rights under pressure, argues Lotje Beek. She envisages a different solution.

title: Noord-Holland wants stricter policy on new data centres
lead: Noord-Holland politicians want stricter rules for the construction of new data centres. The current strategy, which was meant to give more control over the siting of the often large square buildings, is not adequate according to Provinciale Staten (PS). Data centres can circumvent rules by, for example, opting for high-rise buildings and administratively splitting the company into several units.

title: Minute's silence for Bartina Koeman before match against Germany, big banner for new national coach Xavi
lead: Before the Nations League match between the Netherlands and Germany in the Johan Cruijff Arena, a minute's silence was observed on Thursday evening in memory of Bartina Koeman.

title: FC Groningen earn first win in a month against PEC Zwolle
lead: FC Groningen have won a match in the Eredivisie again after more than a month. Coach Dick Lukkien's team were too strong for PEC Zwolle at the Euroborg, winning 3-0.

title: As a queer family you are vulnerable, TV maker Nicolaas Veul (42) knows: 'At the same time I give less of a damn than ever'
Tijn (15) was recruited via Snapchat for a bomb attack: 'They threatened him severely: we are going to rape you, we are going to cut off your fingers'
Dutch national team press conference moved because of Bartina Koeman's funeral
lead: Because of Bartina Koeman's funeral this Wednesday, the Dutch national team is adjusting its programme. The press conference ahead of Nederland-Duitsland has been brought forward, so that players and staff members can pay their last respects to the wife of former national coach Ronald Koeman (63).

title: The prime minister of Singapore is the best-paid leader in the world, and now decides to give away his pay rise
Three arrests after police chase that ends at McDonald's
lead: A police chase ended at the McDrive of a McDonald's along the N65 near Udenhout. The car crashed and caught fire.

title: Ajax player Dolberg out for a longer period with injury sustained with the Danes
lead: Ajax striker Kasper Dolberg picked up a knee injury at a training session of the Danish national team. The Amsterdam club announced this on Tuesday via X. He has left the national team, which is preparing for the Nations League.

title: RTL broadcasts wrong RTL Weer recording with blooper: 'This made no sense'
lead: A small mistake about the weather led to a striking TV moment on Sunday evening. During 'RTL Weer', meteorologist Marc de Jong (56) misspoke, after which he decided to simply do his piece again. The viewer saw it all and then watched him work his way back to the start of his item by flicking through the various weather maps. It turned out that RTL had broadcast the wrong recording.

title: Several shots heard in Roermond: man killed in the street
lead: One person was killed in a shooting in Roermond on Sunday. The incident happened shortly before 22.00 on the Terbaanseweg. The victim is a man, a police spokesperson reports. Nothing further has yet been announced about his identity.

title: Music is being called 'old' ever faster, but young people remain enchanted by it
After losing her mother, art historian Binkie Bloemheuvel (34) wrote her debut novel: 'I see parallels between a bami disc and a Medusa head'
Bron family's dream seemed over after losing 60,000 euros in Ik Vertrek: this is how they are doing now
lead: In 'Ik Vertrek', Robert and Isabelle Bron left with their five children for Germany to convert an old hotel into a Christian group home. They already had the key, but to actually be able to buy the building the family still had to raise 160,000 euros. Robert and Isabelle tell AVROTROS how they are doing now.

title: An officer who goes undercover must dare to lie. 'Do we actually think about the people who do that work?'
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> sometimes works undercover. Criminal law jurist Sophie Naber studied how practice relates to European law. It can "become quicksand".

title: Güner Kuban (1935-2026), operator of club Homolulu, had an untameable, infectious energy: 'She had a very flamboyant life'
Family supports perpetrator of Idaho quadruple murder in challenging life sentence
lead: The family of Bryan Kohberger supports his attempt to withdraw his guilty plea. Last year he confessed to the murder of four students in Idaho. The family says this in a statement to ABC News.

title: Couple from Capelle refuses to be fooled by distraction scam for the second time
lead: A man (78) and a woman (75) from Capelle aan den IJssel have outsmarted a con artist using a distraction scam for the second time. Thanks to their alertness the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> was able to arrest a 28-year-old man from Spijkenisse.

title: Fewer rules or less protection? Europe starts the demolition and the Netherlands eagerly joins in
Five years of DiZa: striving for control over the digital society
lead: The standing parliamentary committee <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-diza">Digitale Zaken</entity> (DiZa) has existed for five years. Reason for Stichting iPoort to invite a panel of six people involved three times to Nieuwspoort in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity> to reflect on the past, present and future of digital affairs.

title: National coach Xavi keeps part of Oranje's foundation and makes changes in some positions: no Depay and Weghorst
lead: New national coach Xavi will use the coming international period to "get to know" players "better". But for all-time top scorer Memphis Depay there is, at this moment, no longer a place.

title: Oranje supporters welcome national coach Xavi with big banner
lead: Before the home match against Germany in the Nations League, supporters of the Dutch national team welcomed the new national coach Xavi Hernández with a big banner. Behind the goal in the Johan Cruijff ArenA, where the core fans 'Dutch Fanatics' sit, a large image of the Spaniard could be seen. 'Xavi, welkom' was written with it.

title: NVWA illegal timber team seizes 375 tonnes of wood at importer
lead: At an importer of tropical hardwood, 375 tonnes of 'illegal timber' have been seized. The azobé wood comes from Gabon. According to the Nederlandse Voedsel- en Warenautoriteit (NVWA), the importer cannot demonstrate that the trees it comes from were legally felled.

title: Ten years of VAR: a 'great safety net' that still provokes a lot of anger
Further increase in traffic fines meets opposition from Raad van State
lead: The Raad van State is critical of the plan by justice minister <entity id="person:david-van-weel">David van Weel</entity> (VVD) to let traffic fines for minor offences rise with inflation. The cabinet adviser stresses that traffic fines have risen much more sharply in recent years than fines for serious offences.

title: State buys shares in Borssele nuclear power plant from Zeeland governments
lead: The Dutch state is buying 70 percent of the shares of EPZ, the operator of the nuclear power plant in the Zeeland village of Borssele. The aim of the takeover is to keep the nuclear power plant open longer.

title: Donny Roelvink supports brother Dave after breakup: 'He is very sad'
lead: Donny Roelvink (28) is standing by his brother Dave (32) now that his relationship with Marijn Kuipers (26) is over. Donny notices that Dave is 'very sad'.

title: More shops must accept deposit returns in fight against litter
lead: It must become possible to return used cans and plastic bottles with a deposit in many more shops. Minister Stientje van <entity id="org:gemeente-veldhoven">Veldhoven</entity> of Economic Affairs and Climate is thinking of a threshold somewhere between 43 and 50 square metres of sales floor area, she writes to the Tweede Kamer. Smaller shops will be exempted.

title: More dismissals due to bankruptcies and reorganisations
lead: In 2025, 8.1% of dismissed employees lost their jobs for business economic reasons. That is one and a half times as many as three years earlier.

title: New government service to spot foreign interference
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> is working on a government service that is to counter interference by foreign organisations in public debate. The bill for it will be submitted in the course of next year. At the elections for the water boards and provinces, next March, a trial is already to be carried out with it.

title: Bureau Groningen on its way: meet the twelve officers
lead: Ewout Genemans (41) is diving into police life once again. This time the presenter travels to the north of the country for 'Bureau Groningen'. On Instagram he introduces the twelve officers whom viewers will follow in the coming season.

title: Jutta Leerdam wanted to quit skating when mother fell ill: 'We thought it was the end of the story'
lead: Jutta Leerdam (27) considered ending her skating career when her mother got oesophageal cancer. In 'Casa di Beau' the skater tells how that difficult period made her doubt her future on the ice.

title: The world a haunted house
lead: The scariest haunted house I ever experienced was not crawling with dancing skeletons and suddenly rising vampires. No, it made use of my own fear.

title: Meta's Muse makes AI helper popular with consumers
lead: Tech group Meta appears to be the first to have made a successful agent AI that can independently carry out tasks for consumers. Mark Zuckerberg's company is making leaps on the stock market.

title: From stage to wedding room: Gordon takes a new path as babs
lead: Today Gordon (58) was not at a wedding with a microphone in his hand to sing a song, but as a wedding officiant. The singer and newly minted babs conducted his first marriage today and tells RTL Boulevard that more weddings are in the pipeline.

title: Spanish national coach De la Fuente extends contract until after Euro 2032
lead: MADRID (ANP/RTR) - Spain's national coach Luis de la Fuente has extended his contract with the Spanish football federation (RFEF) up to and including the European Championship of 2032. The RFEF announced this. The 65-year-old coach won, among other things, the last World Cup with Spain.

title: When all the signals turn red
lead: When I was about to make a long train journey through the Netherlands this summer, I remembered that MP Habtamu de Hoop (PRO) had arranged free train tickets for those who otherwise could not go on holiday because of rising oil prices. On the NS website I found Nederland Dal Vrij for 49 euros per month. Not a bargain, but still a nice deal.

title: Help, I don't want a dog!
FVD member of the Eerste Kamer was at far-right protest on the Malieveld
lead: FVD Eerste Kamer member Eric Kemperman was present on Saturday at the far-right protest on the Malieveld in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity>. FVD had in fact indicated beforehand that it did not support the protest. Another FVD member had withdrawn for that reason.

title: Nicolette van Dam receives spicy DMs, while it stays quiet for Bas Smit
lead: Bas Smit (45) and Nicolette van Dam (41) have been together for twenty years, but that does not stop some men from sending striking messages to Nicolette. In the podcast 'Lightless Lounge' Bas says that her DMs regularly fill up with spicy requests and dick pics. For him, on the other hand, it stays remarkably quiet.

title: VNG: more money and clear frameworks from national government needed for youth care reform
lead: Youth care in the Netherlands is not doing well, according to piles of studies and reports. To improve youth care structurally, the Hervormingsagenda Jeugd was established in 2023. The VNG examined where municipalities now stand when it comes to achieving that agenda. What is needed to bring this to a successful conclusion in 2028? From the national government more money and clear frameworks are needed, at regional and municipal level mainly more people and better…

title: 'Whoever wins AI wins', says Trump, and that is why he and Xi want nothing to do with stricter regulation
lead: China and the United States are locked in a fierce competitive battle in the field of artificial intelligence. Although concerns about its dangers are growing, there is little chance that presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump will make agreements this week about controlling it.

title: André Dongelmans shows huge transformation during weight-loss journey
lead: André Dongelmans (39) shares a new update on his weight-loss process on Instagram. After 25 weeks the counter stands at 73.5 kilos, which means that the actor has now lost 23.5 kilos. In recent weeks he stuck less strictly to his regime, but to his relief his weight remained fairly stable.

title: Painful for the EU and Ukraine: two Russian oligarchs removed from the sanctions list
Help, a disciplinary complaint against you: 'Not a single critical question was asked of the complainants'
lead: What does it do to you when a disciplinary complaint is filed against you? Three professionals tell their story. 'It frustrated me that someone had just written down all kinds of untruths about me.'

title: Radio DJ Jeske van Trigt gets a regular show on 100% NL
lead: Radio DJ Jeske van Trigt (26) is getting her own regular show on 100% NL. The radio station announced this on Wednesday. From 25 September the radio DJ can be heard on 100% NL every Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Jeske previously had her own show on SLAM!, but already regularly filled in at 100% NL.

title: Bayern München thrash Union Berlin, Saibari scores
lead: Bayern München have also won the third home match of this season by a wide margin. The reigning national champions beat Union Berlin 7-0 in the German league. At half-time it was already 3-0. Ismael Saibari, who came over from PSV, scored his first goal for Bayern as a substitute.

title: Journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico admitted to the White House again after all
Call for structural funding for foundation problems

title: Odyssey
lead: Since Homer we have known that people can form a coalition for different reasons: Menelaus wanted his wife back, Agamemnon sought power and prestige, Achilles longed for eternal fame and Odysseus was forced by an oath to take part. They went to war together, not because they had the same ideals, but because their interests temporarily overlapped. A present-day coalition, too, is rarely the product of a shared conviction.

lead: Captain Virgil van Dijk quickly decided to continue longer as an international after a conversation with the new national coach Xavi Hernández. The 35-year-old defender says this on Monday in conversation with ESPN.

title: Jordy and Lisanne confirm Mae's fear in De Bondgenoten: 'Will be a tough month for her'
lead: Mae is afraid that not everyone likes her in 'De Bondgenoten'. When Jordy and Lisanne discuss their feelings about Mae, that fear does not seem entirely unfounded. 'De Bondgenoten' can be seen Monday to Saturday at 19.30 on SBS6.

title: NEC draws with Go Ahead Eagles after early lead
lead: NEC also failed to beat Go Ahead Eagles in the Eredivisie. Last season's number 3 got no further than a draw in their own stadium: 1-1.

title: Extremely expensive panda is ideal diplomatic tool for China
lead: Pandas have been used by China in political negotiations for years. In the past the country gave them away, nowadays they come with a hefty price tag. This week president Xi Jinping is visiting America and the big question is whether he will once again use his pandas as a trump card.

title: Artist Michiel Voet on De pionier: 'Confusion is a great starting point to activate thinking'
Trump threatens in UN speech to 'destroy' Iran
lead: American President Donald Trump threatens to 'destroy' Iran if the country does not quickly close a deal with the US. He also calls on all countries to leave the International Criminal Court in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity> immediately.

title: Fortunately there are the government's cleaners, who simply clear up all the Prinsjesdag mess
Cabinet helps evacuate sick children from Gaza, but not to the Netherlands
lead: Several hundred seriously ill Palestinian children will be evacuated from Gaza with financial help from the Netherlands for medical treatment in Jordan. Minister for Ontwikkelingssamenwerking Sjoerdsma (D66) announced this. There will be no medical evacuations to the Netherlands. According to Sjoerdsma, far more children can be helped in the region with the same money than if they are brought to the Netherlands.

title: 200,000 people in Germany take to the streets over wave of layoffs in the car industry
lead: In Germany large strikes took place yesterday over a wave of layoffs in the car industry. Almost 200,000 employees stopped work and took to the streets.

title: French public prosecutor opens investigation into PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaïfi
lead: The French <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> has opened an investigation into PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaïfi for conflict of interest. The French news agency AFP reports this. The investigation into the Qatari relates to his dual role as president of the Paris football club and of beIN Media Group during negotiations on broadcasting rights of the French football federation.

title: Criminals take over homes of vulnerable people
lead: More than 50 municipalities are dealing with criminals who misuse the homes of vulnerable people for drug crime. Housing corporations are very concerned about this development. More and more vulnerable people live in social rental homes, and so the risk of criminal exploitation rises, according to municipalities, <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and housing corporations.

title: Jade Kops' sister struggles with life that goes on: 'My world stands still'
lead: It is five months since Jade Kops died at the age of 19 from the effects of cancer. On Instagram her mother and sister Amber reflect on the loss and on a life that has changed for good for them.

title: Colosseum closed after fatal accident, tourists angry: 'Holiday ruined'
lead: In Rome a 22-year-old man has died during work in the Colosseum. The Italian top attraction is therefore closed today. Visitors are not happy about it.

title: Will Koopman dives into the periwig era with new series full of young talent
lead: After successes such as 'Gooische Vrouwen', 'Familie Kruys' and 'Oogappels', a new series from director Will Koopman (69) is coming soon. In the absurd comic drama 'Met de Franse Slag' the makers take a completely different tack and we follow four women during the periwig era.

title: Whoever stands in the way of bunq founder Ali Niknam must give way, a biography shows: 'For Ali everything is about efficiency, never about empathy for another'
Colosseum closed after fatal accident, tourists not happy
lead: The Colosseum in Rome is closed all day because of a fatal workplace accident involving a technician. A 22-year-old man fell ten metres last night while working on a new lighting installation. Visitors are reacting with displeasure to the unexpected closure.

title: Dutch marines explore Greenland for the first time: 'Even rougher and more challenging'
lead: Dutch marines had never trained in Greenland before. But now that the area is becoming strategically ever more important because of melting ice, and America threatened in recent months to annex it, it was high time to take a look.

title: FIFA boss Infantino: culture of dialogue is needed
lead: FIFA president Gianni Infantino says he is open to open discussions about possible reforms at the world football federation. "There must be a culture of dialogue, of listening to each other and respecting each other. It is not about generating positive headlines, it is about doing what is right for the sport", he wrote on Instagram with a video showing him visiting the Arabian Gulf Cup in Saudi Arabia.

title: Who are the Amsterdammers having a private swimming pool built under their house? 'Neighbourhoods that were already rich are now going to super-rich'
Football federation president wins elections massively ignored by Moroccans
lead: Fouzi Lekjaa has been the Moroccan minister of budget affairs since 2021. Fewer than a quarter of eligible voters turned up at the polls.

title: Jan G. from Overasselt arrested for importing 4000 kilos of cocaine
lead: The 28-year-old Jan G. from Overasselt has been arrested by the German <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> along the A44 motorway near the German town of Soest. Sources confirm this to RTL Nieuws. G. is suspected of involvement in an attempt to import almost 4000 kilos of cocaine.

title: National coach Xavi faces a complex task: he wants a metamorphosis to dominant football, with a team that has shortcomings
lead: The new national coach Xavi wants Oranje to play attacking and energetic football. The question is how much of that will already be visible in his debut on Thursday against Germany. "We will take the initiative. We will be defensively brave."

title: Dries Roelvink does not leave Dave alone 'for a minute' after break-up: 'We stand behind him'
lead: Dries Roelvink (67) is supporting his son Dave (32) now that his relationship with Marijn Kuipers (26) is over. Dave announced the break-up last week and can count on his father's support in this difficult period.

title: Criticism of photo of Queen Máxima with controversial Syrian president: 'Where is the line?'
lead: As a UN figurehead, Queen Máxima (55) is making a special visit to America this week. There she is speaking to champion her special field: financial health. But there was one thing the queen had not counted on. And that is all the criticism of a photo with the Syrian president, who used to be seen as a jihadist terrorist.

title: Province was not allowed to require municipality to take drone flights into account
lead: The <entity id="org:provincie-flevoland">provincie Flevoland</entity> should not have prohibited the <entity id="org:gemeente-noordoostpolder">gemeente Noordoostpolder</entity> from including rules in the environmental plan that would hamper testing with drones in Marknesse. This is shown by a ruling of the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity>.

title: Autumn begins calm and mostly dry with possibly 22 degrees this afternoon
lead: Last night at 02.05 the astronomical autumn officially began. There are roughly two kinds of autumn weather: stormy and wet weather, or calm and dry weather. We will see the latter in the coming period, with pleasant temperatures.

title: Rijk Hofman reveals reason behind end of podcast BROERS
lead: The sudden end of the podcast 'BROERS' in May 2025 came as a surprise to many listeners. More than a year after the last episode, Rijk Hofman (29) explains in the podcast 'Guncle' why he and his brother Sam Hofman (30) decided to stop.

title: Municipalities, make women's health a topic of discussion
lead: A&O fonds Gemeenten calls on municipal management, HR and occupational health professionals to put women's health on the agenda as part of good employership. Their Personeelsmonitor Gemeenten 2025 shows that the municipal sector is 56 percent female and that absenteeism among women is structurally higher than among men: 8.6 versus 6 percent. 'That is why we believe municipal organisations should have the conversation: make women's health and prevention a topic of discussion.'

title: ASML doubles number of employees with new campus
lead: ASML this week celebrates the start of construction of a new campus, which represents the chip machine maker's substantial expansion near <entity id="org:gemeente-eindhoven">Eindhoven</entity>. The new location ensures that important activities of the high-tech company remain in the region. The intention is that the expansion will accommodate some 20,000 extra jobs, which almost doubles the number of employees in the Netherlands.

title: Queen Camilla to appear soon in new BBC documentary
lead: British Queen Camilla (79) will soon be seen in 'The Book That Changed My Life', a BBC documentary about the influence books can have on people. The British broadcaster announced this on Saturday.

title: Joost Eerdmans' about-turn on day one of the Politieke Beschouwingen leads to confusion in the Kamer
lead: For two days the Tweede Kamer is debating the Prinsjesdag budget. The surprise of day one: according to JA21, <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> no longer has to choose between going left or going right. Support can also be given 'per subject'.

title: What about the cows?
lead: Columnist Marjoleine de Vos is in Burgundy and sees the consequences of climate change. She herself has taken measures to live more sustainably. "Do I believe it helps? Mmm. But I do believe in mass. The more people who do not lose heart, the greater the chance that something will still happen."

title: Skewed renting: moving on to nowhere
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> has a new solution for the housing shortage: making people who already have a home pay more. According to the new cabinet plan, housing corporations must from now on require tenants with a higher income to pay 50 or 100 euros extra rent per month every year, until the maximum rent under the points system is reached. About 177,000 households […] Read more posts on Sargasso

title: Broccoli with cashew butter and noodles
Dream collaboration comes true for Qlas with brand-new track
lead: Qlas's brand-new track is out. On the track he works with two artists he greatly admires: Boef and Antoon. The emotional song is the follow-up to his big hit 'Waar Was Je?' and once again shows a personal and sensitive side of Qlas.

title: Surprise in the Tweede Kamer: lower tax on gas turns out not to be possible
lead: Many parties are concerned about the rising energy bills of households, but the solutions are not easy to come by. For example, the tax on natural gas turns out not to be able to go down next year, because of agreements that the Netherlands itself made with Brussels.

title: Giel Beelen looks forward to new radio show: 'Really going to happen'
lead: Giel Beelen (49) had already whispered it himself, but from Friday you kick off the weekend with the radio DJ. Giel is returning to Radio Veronica and he cannot wait to start.

title: There is no river that brings us so much, but the Rhine is tired
lead: The water level of the Rhine has never been as low as it was this summer. While we depend on the river for the economy. Are we not asking too much of it?

title: Peruvians wanted to smuggle drugs via luggage on KLM flight to Amsterdam
lead: Baggage handlers in Peru tried earlier this month to put packages of cocaine into suitcases. It possibly concerned luggage of unsuspecting travellers who were being flown to Schiphol on a KLM flight. In Amsterdam a 37-year-old Peruvian has been arrested.

title: Veerman wants to put the past behind him after return to Oranje
lead: Joey Veerman no longer wants to look back on the past after his return to Oranje. The midfielder was no longer called up by Ronald Koeman after the 2024 European Championship in Germany and now, more than two years later, under the new national coach Xavi Hernández, is part of the Dutch national team squad again for the first time.

title: The far right is confused: asylum is no longer the theme
Bauke Mollema rides world championships in Montréal 'because he had to be there anyway': 'So why would I not ride too?'
lead: One moment in a suit and tie as ambassador for the world championships in <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity> and <entity id="org:provincie-drenthe">Drenthe</entity>, the next moment in orange on the bike. These are special days in Montréal for Bauke Mollema, who without his role at the UCI congress might not even have taken part in the world championships.

title: Twilight actor Taylor Lautner and wife Taylor welcome daughter with a very fitting name
lead: Taylor Lautner (34) has become a father for the first time. His wife Taylor (29), who since her marriage to the actor is also called Taylor Lautner, gave birth to a daughter last week.

title: Douwe Bob breathes new life into De beste singer-songwriter van Nederland: 'So much talent around'
lead: Douwe Bob (33) and Giel Beelen (49) are working on a return of the talent show 'De beste singer-songwriter van Nederland'. Whether that will also be on TV is not yet known. "We'll see who takes part", the singer said on Friday in the RTL 4 talk show 'Renze'.

title: Eigenaren in Nederland moeten katten vanaf 2028 chippen om aantal zwerfkatten te verminderen
lead: De Nederlandse regering is van plan het chippen van huiskatten verplicht te maken vanaf 1 januari 2028.

title: Ed Sheeran says 'sorry' and calls situation in Gaza 'indefensible'
lead: The British pop star Ed Sheeran has said that the situation in Gaza is 'indefensible', after he received a wave of criticism. Rapper Macklemore was dropped as Sheeran's opening act for pro-Palestinian statements during the show.

title: Real Madrid captain Valverde suffers ankle injury
lead: MADRID (ANP/AFP) - Real Madrid captain Federico Valverde has sprained his left ankle. The club from the Spanish capital announced this on Tuesday. The Uruguay international sustained the injury on Sunday during the lost match at Atlético Madrid (2-1).

title: Ben Saunders' family not attending funeral 'after long and intensive consultation'
lead: Ben Saunders' family will not be present at his funeral tomorrow. The family says so in a statement. According to them the choice was made out of love for Ben. They also ask for understanding and respect for their decision.

title: Mayor of Ede shocked by scale of care fraud
lead: Mayor <entity id="person:rene-verhulst">René Verhulst</entity> of the <entity id="org:gemeente-ede">gemeente Ede</entity> is shocked by the scale of care fraud in the eastern Netherlands. Phenomenon research by the RIEC Oost-Nederland into criminal money flows in care shows that in the period 2020-2024 no less than 71 million euros in suspicious transactions took place in the sector.

title: Ilse DeLange makes Top 40 comeback after 18 years with So Incredible: 'No words for it'
lead: Anyone who thought that 'So Incredible' by Ilse DeLange (49) was by now mainly a nostalgic song is mistaken. Exactly 18 years after the original release, the hit is returning to the Top 40 thanks to a considerable rise on TikTok. This week Ilse is at number sixteen with the song and can hardly believe it herself. She tells RTL Boulevard this.

title: No beds, but hotdogs: this is what you will find in the small IKEA
lead: IKEA will soon open smaller stores closer to populated areas, roughly the size of a large supermarket. So no endless rows of sofas, beds and kitchens, but what will you be able to buy there?

title: Fallen PKK fighters are openly commemorated, and that is a sensitive matter in Turkey
lead: For the first time, PKK fighters who died during the conflict are being publicly commemorated in Turkish cities. That provokes resistance among some Turks. The Kurds present show their grief and their support for the PKK. "We are proud. We are sad. We hold our heads high and carry on."

title: Paris attacker in isolation cell for almost 10 years, and it will stay that way for a while
lead: Jihadist Salah Abdeslam may not leave the isolation cell. He tried to force this through the court in the French city of Lille, but it did not agree. Abdeslam has been in solitary confinement for almost ten years.

title: Van der Poel rides 175 kilometres alone and wins: 'Don't know what got into me'
lead: Mathieu van der Poel has won the last stage of the Tour of Luxembourg. And how. Van der Poel went off at the start of the final stage, and no one saw him again. In the end he rode 175 kilometres alone.

title: Zelensky reports deal for delivery of badly needed Patriot air defence missiles
lead: Ukraine will get a new batch of Patriot air defence missiles, President Volodymyr Zelensky reports. An agreement on this was signed on Thursday. On Facebook, Zelensky leaves open with whom. He speaks of an "important decision."

title: Défano Holwijn fights for LGBTI acceptance: 'A rainbow does no harm'
lead: Influencer Défano Holwijn (34) has stood up for the queer community in a video on Instagram. In it he says, among other things, that homosexuality is not corona and is not contagious, but that some people behave as if 'the freedom, visibility, or presence of homosexual people takes something away from them'. He then wonders aloud what that is supposed to be.

title: Supporting role for Vollering and Nooijen in World Championship time trial, Reusser wins again
lead: Cyclists Demi Vollering and Lieke Nooijen did not come close to a medal at the world time trial championship in Montreal. The Swiss Marlen Reusser lived up to her role as favourite and convincingly defended her title; Vollering finished eighth and Nooijen twelfth. Vollering in particular was considered a candidate for the podium after her earlier World Championship silver (2024) and bronze (2025).

title: Pension transition for aldermen raises questions about regulatory burden
lead: With the introduction of the new pension system, the pensions of political office holders are being placed with pension fund ABP. But how much regulatory burden that transition entails has not been mapped out, according to the Adviescollege toetsing regeldruk (ATR). There is also no insight into how many pension beneficiaries will be affected by the transition.

title: Nail-biting for CDU in German state, party risks missing the electoral threshold
lead: The radical-right party AfD has made substantial gains in the German state elections in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, the exit poll and first projections show. This while the German Christian Democrats fall below the electoral threshold of 5 percent in a projection for the first time. A low point for the party. In Berlin, Die Linke is clearly becoming the largest party according to the projections.

title: Jetten waarschuwt Trump dat hij de betrekkingen 'in gevaar brengt' vanwege ICC
lead: Minister-president <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> heeft gezegd dat de Nederlanders op diplomatiek vlak alles uit de kast halen om verdere sancties te voorkomen...

title: Denmark already banned them, but can agriculture do without pfas pesticides?
lead: Potato farmers are at risk of losing another fungicide, now that concerns about the pfas variant TFA are growing. 'Growing becomes a lottery.'

title: Son of prince Laurent kept his origins secret for years: 'Knew it since I was sixteen'
lead: Clément Vandenkerckhove (26) already knew at sixteen that prince Laurent (62) is his biological father. Yet he kept it to himself for years. In the Flemish programme 'Zeg eens euh' he says that only one person around him knew the secret: his best friend.

title: Wedding bells for MEAU: singer engaged to guitarist Vadim
lead: MEAU (26) and her boyfriend, guitarist Vadim, are getting married. The singer shares the news on Instagram and immediately shows that the engagement has already been well celebrated. Together with their loved ones, the couple toasted the next step in their relationship.

title: Gelderland is the first province to establish nitrogen strips
lead: Gelderland is definitively establishing strips of 500 metres around the Veluwe and three other vulnerable nature areas, where nitrogen emissions must come down sharply. A majority of the Provinciale Staten (37-14) chose on Wednesday evening to lay that down in the new environmental ordinance.

title: Forgot your groceries? Jason (12) and Sam (10) will cycle to the supermarket for you
lead: For residents of Pijnacker, the supermarket service of Jason (12) and Sam (10) is a godsend. Forgot the eggs for the omelette? Or have your hands in the marinade and discover that the garlic is still missing? The young entrepreneurs will quickly cycle to the supermarket for you. "At first we charged 30 cents for it."

title: NPO makes decision on participation in Eurovision Song Contest 2027: the Netherlands takes part
lead: It is out in the open: the Netherlands will take part in the Eurovision Song Contest 2027. Sources told RTL Boulevard this on Wednesday. This ends months of uncertainty about Dutch participation.

title: King Haakon closes sailing season on royal ship
lead: King Haakon of Norway on Thursday closed the sailing season of the royal ship Norge. It was one of his first public duties since he became king at the end of last month.

title: Investigation into footballer Xhaka over alleged fake COVID certificates
lead: LUZERN (ANP/DPA) - The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> of Luzern has started an investigation into footballer Granit Xhaka, the captain of Sunderland and the Swiss national team, on suspicion of obtaining fake COVID vaccination certificates. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> of Luzern confirmed this to news agency DPA.

title: Citizens and bureaucracy heading for an AI showdown
lead: Former alderman Luc Volders of the <entity id="org:gemeente-meerssen">gemeente Meerssen</entity> is enthusiastic about what AI can do for governments. While AI is ignored in many local election manifestos, he sets out in an essay how municipalities can save millions. Among his proposals are an AI chatbot for the Klant Contact Centrum, AI for drafting council documents, and AI for permit screening, fraud detection and the handling of Woo requests.

title: Van Gerwen loses in first round of World Series of Darts
lead: Michael van Gerwen has been knocked out in the first round of the World Series of Darts Finals. The 37-year-old Dutch defending champion lost 6-5 to Northern Irishman Daryl Gurney in the AFAS Live in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>.

title: Gouden Griffel 2026 for deceased writer Sjoerd Kuyper
lead: Sjoerd Kuyper has won the Gouden Griffel 2026 for his book Maantje verhuist de zee, book trade body CPNB announced on Thursday. The writer died on Tuesday at the age of 74. Before that he still received the prize in the presence of his wife and publisher.

title: PFAS levels too high in tap water in Noord- and Zuid-Holland
lead: Tap water in large parts of Noord- and Zuid-Holland contains more PFAS than the Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu (<entity id="org:rijksinstituut-voor-volksgezondheid-en-milieu">RIVM</entity>) advises. Greenpeace concludes this in an analysis of data from the ten Dutch drinking water companies. High PFAS levels occur particularly in <entity id="org:provincie-noord-holland">Noord-Holland</entity>.

title: Monica Bellucci and Richard Gere guests of honour at Prince Albert's party
lead: Actors Monica Bellucci (61) and Richard Gere (77) were present as guests of honour on Friday evening at the celebration of the twentieth anniversary of the Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation, Prince Albert's foundation. On Instagram, the Monegasque court looks back on the festive evening.

title: Former head of detectives furious about release of suspect in school camp tragedy: 'This cannot be, this must not be'
lead: That a 20-year-old suspect is sent home after the traffic tragedy near Vogelwaarde to await his trial is unbearable for the bereaved. Former head of detectives Sander Schaepman understands the frustration and incomprehension in Zeeuws-Vlaanderen like no other. "This cannot be, this must not be. Our legal system is really failing here."

title: Fireworks and glass thrown during anti-asylum centre protest in Opheusden
lead: A protest against a possible asylum seekers' centre in Opheusden turned into riots on Thursday evening. Demonstrators threw fireworks and glass at officers, four police officers were injured and fourteen people were arrested.

title: US opens attack on the Criminal Court: consequences could be major
lead: No more money for investigations into war crimes, which would therefore come to a standstill. That could be the result of new American sanctions against the International Criminal Court. Sources tell Reuters and the Wall Street Journal that the US will come with sanctions against the court very shortly, and that could have major consequences.

title: Lace in menswear: 'There is a need for decoration in life'
lead: Blouses and trousers with lace, surely only women wear those? No, author Dorothé Duijves saw when she visited several festivals last summer where popular male artists dressed in lace clothing.

title: Martijn van Eijzeren, known as Stuntkabouter, tested positive for cocaine after fatal accident
lead: Martijn van Eijzeren (28), known as Stuntkabouter and from the Eurovision act of Joost Klein (28), tested positive for cocaine after the fatal car accident in France in which director Ilya Vierhout was killed. The French newspaper Le Dauphiné Libéré reports this on Thursday. According to the newspaper, Van Eijzeren is formally suspected of causing a fatal accident under the influence of narcotics.

title: Angela Groothuizen ready for Sexy Sixty show after turbulent period: 'Right on time'
lead: Life energy, staying curious and lots of dancing; three of the many themes that Angela Groothuizen (66) puts centre stage in her new theatre show 'Sexy Sixty'. The singer worked towards it for a long time, but is bringing the interactive show to Dutch theatres at the right moment in her life, she tells the ANP. "I approach it much more curiously and calmly than in the years before. This time it feels like: 'hey, it is exactly on time'", Angela explains.

title: Alderman Esmah Lahlah (46) has only just moved to the city, but is already taking part in the Groot Amsterdams Dictee: 'It fits my induction programme'
Iris Hond tries her hand at film music for the first time
lead: Iris Hond (39) has written the music for a film for the first time. The pianist and composer proudly shares on Instagram that she created the film score for the historical drama 'SPINOZA', the latest film by director Rudolf van den Berg.

title: 'Symbol of the housing crisis': 87-year-old woman evicted in Madrid after seventy years
lead: On a stretcher, after seventy years in the same house: that is how 87-year-old Maricarmen left her apartment in the Madrid district of Retiro today after all. The woman was not even given a few hours to pack her belongings, despite a night full of protest, tear gas and police violence.

title: The Indonesian jungle falls silent through the mass capture of wild songbirds
Can your skin become addicted to cream, and when is applying it actually necessary?
'What if the Netherlands were to send an artist of Palestinian descent?'
Vijlbrief, stop the false promise behind shortening WW
lead: And then suddenly the emperor had no clothes on. Halving the WW is being sold by <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> as a means of getting more people into work. But 8000 extra jobs is really too few to justify such a drastic intervention, writes our political reporter Laurens Kok.

title: Arnhem recruits via municipal pool. 'We hire the person'
lead: Daniël Gerritsen slides two brochures across. The first introduces the neighbourhood manager. The second publication is a small information guide for residents of Arnhem in 'his' neighbourhoods Sint Marten and Klarendal in Arnhem, partly compiled by him. Damp and mould problems in the house, whose door do they knock on then? Who are the community police officers and neighbourhood caretakers? But also: where can they take guitar lessons?

title: Persistent pressure on capital market drives interest rates up further
lead: The strength of the American and European economies is fuelling concerns about higher inflation and more interest rate hikes by central banks. Worldwide, capital market interest rates are rising further.

title: Opinion: Tens of thousands of asylum seekers are stuck here and cannot protest
Clen V. disputes investigation into murder of girlfriend: 'It is a very strange case'
lead: Many will surely still remember the two ABN AMRO employees who died shortly after each other. Today Clen V., the partner of one of the women, is back in court. He is suspected of murder and poisoning. Clen V. is also known for his participation in the dating show 'Lang Leve de Liefde'.

title: Lidl may no longer sell imitation Birkenstocks in the Netherlands
lead: The supermarket group Lidl may no longer sell fake Birkenstocks in the Netherlands. The court decided this on Wednesday. For every day that sales of the sandals continue, Lidl must pay the sandal maker 5000 euros.

title: 'Friendly weather' in the coming days and temperatures remain high
lead: The weather does not look bad in the coming days. This morning an area of (drizzle) rain moves away to the south-east. After that the sun comes out regularly. In the night to Wednesday there is a high chance of dense fog. Later on Wednesday a few showers follow from the west.

title: Facial recognition in Moscow: convenient payment, but your data ends up with the Russian government
lead: A ride on the metro, or buying a cup of coffee at the station? In Moscow you no longer need a card to pay, not even a phone. You look at a camera that recognises your face and the money is automatically debited from your account. But you are also constantly being watched.

title: Fairground worker dies after accident with Oktoberfest ride in Munich
lead: In Munich in Germany a 52-year-old employee of an Oktoberfest fairground ride was killed on Monday evening. According to the Süddeutsche Zeitung the man worked at the Hangover, a free-fall tower about 85 metres high.

title: Brobbey scores three times for losing Sunderland
lead: Brian Brobbey will report to the Dutch national team on Monday, presumably with a lot of confidence. The 24-year-old Sunderland forward scored no fewer than three times in the away match against leaders Manchester City. It was not enough for a positive result, because Manchester City scored five goals: 5-3.

title: Restriction on Suurhoffbrug costs transport sector '600,000 euros per day'
lead: The restrictions on road traffic on the Suurhoffbrug in the Rotterdam port cost the transport sector 'hundreds of thousands per day' in damage. According to an initial estimate by Deltalinqs, which represents the interests of companies in the Rotterdam port area, it amounts to 600,000 euros per day.

title: Jay Zwarts screams in pain after hard fall in Good Luck Guys
lead: During a game in 'Good Luck Guys' things go badly wrong for Jay Zwarts. He takes a hard fall, after which the medical team immediately springs into action and the other contestants are left shocked.

title: Scale jump
lead: Figures matter, just like words. And yet a number without context does not always tell us as much. In the world of municipalities, the threshold of 100,000 inhabitants is such a number: the so-called scale jump. As soon as you pass that threshold, supposedly all sorts of things change. But let's be honest: the asphalt certainly does not change colour as soon as inhabitant 100,001 registers at the counter. And yet that threshold exists for a reason. A municipality with that number of inhabitants is viewed differently, and really does work differently.

title: Did angry alderman throw a laptop at the mayor? Politicians in Wassenaar want answers
lead: The Wassenaar municipal council is gripped by a possible piquant clash. Alderman Laurens van Doeveren is said to have thrown a laptop at mayor Leendert de Lange in a fit of rage. That story is known to several councillors, and councillor Ben Paulides is now making it public. However, it is complete nonsense, the mayor says in an urgent statement.

title: No doubts at Audi: continuing with Bortoleto and Hülkenberg in F1
lead: BAKU (ANP/AFP) - The Formula 1 team Audi will have the same line-up in 2027 as this year. Team boss Mattia Binotto confirmed at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in Baku that the German Nico Hülkenberg and the Brazilian Gabriel Bortoleto will stay with the German team.

title: Robert van Hemert lost his voice from many performances: 'Really killing'
lead: It was quiet around Robert van Hemert (33) for a while. Voice problems kept him off the stage for some time, but the folk singer is back. Together with the Bankzitters he launched his new single 'Rapido', and as if that were not enough, he has also moved house. RTL Boulevard came over for coffee and a big tour of his new home.

title: Import and sales ban on goods from occupied Palestinian territories, this is what it means
lead: Importing dates, avocados and pomegranates from the occupied Palestinian territories is banned as of today. These goods may no longer come onto the Dutch market. Why did the cabinet introduce this ban and how will they enforce it? Political reporter Roel Schreinemachers answers these and other important questions about the trade ban.

title: The world lives on credit. How dangerous is that? A lesson in bond markets
lead: Countries worldwide are taking on more and more debt. But since this summer the interest rates on those debts have also been rising.

title: New Gooische Vrouwen trailer reveals: Cheryl Morero misses 'nightly adventures'
lead: After a long wait, the time has almost come: the friends of 'Gooische Vrouwen' return for a new season. The first images can now be seen and one thing is clear: things will not stay quiet in the Gooi this time either.

title: Man shot dead in Roermond, police looking for witnesses
lead: In Roermond, one person was killed in a shooting last night.

title: Municipalities get budget for strengthening vital processes
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het Kabinet</entity>-Jetten is freeing up money for the resilience of municipalities against hybrid and military threats. In 2027 they get 20 million, in 2028 they get 25 million and the amount rises to 60 million in 2031. The money is intended to give municipalities concrete support for 'Resilience and recovery capacity at local level'.

title: ABP invests 1 billion in fast-growing companies
lead: ABP, the largest pension fund in the Netherlands, expects to invest approximately 1 billion euros in young, promising European companies over the next three years. ABP confirms this following reports by the FD and the <entity id="org:rwt-nederlandse-omroep-stichting-nos">NOS</entity>. Initially, the pension fund will put 250 million euros into the Scaleup Europe Fund, a fund focused on investments in European technology companies.

title: How did Gouda manage to become a hub of tapestry production in the 17th century?
lead: New research reveals Gouda's central place in tapestry weaving in the Low Countries. Museum Gouda shows some spectacular examples of it.

title: Prime minister Jetten on falling gay acceptance: 'Shocking figures'
lead: Prime minister Jetten (D66) finds it 'shocking' that the acceptance of homosexuality among young people has fallen sharply. He points to the influence of social media and wants to see whether <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> can 'hold social media companies to account more strictly'. The prime minister, who is himself in a relationship with a man, also notices that online hatred of gay people has increased considerably.

title: Why is male Hollywood suddenly wearing Chanel?
Hundreds of uniforms thrown away every week because of forgotten ballpoint pens, hospital makes appeal
lead: Every week hundreds of uniforms are thrown away in Dutch hospitals because pens or markers go into the washing machine with them. That is the finding of a survey by RTL Nieuws. The result? Not snow-white but blue suits, ready for the bin. The UMC <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity> is now making an urgent but simple appeal to staff: check your trouser and coat pockets more carefully.

title: Earl Spencer's book about sister Princess Diana disappoints: 'Not sensational'
lead: The book by Earl Spencer (62), the brother of Princess Diana, which comes out on Tuesday, has been causing an earthquake in Great Britain all week. But Earl is far from done talking. On Sunday the American <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">CBS</entity> published an explosive interview with the aristocratic scandal writer.

title: Marijn Kuipers cannot handle 'crap' on social media: 'Already have enough on my mind'
lead: Marijn Kuipers (26) is 'currently handling badly' the negative reactions she receives on social media. The influencer writes this in a post on Instagram. Normally, by her own account, she 'never' engages 'with that kind of thing', but now she is making an exception. 'Live and let live.'

title: Felix Meurders (80) presents very last broadcast of Kassa
lead: The very last broadcast of 'Kassa' will be presented in December by Felix Meurders (80). He takes over the presenting from Amber Kortzorg (35), who will then be on maternity leave. The presenter revealed this on Thursday on the <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> 1 talk show 'Pauw & De Wit'.

title: Experts call for openness about Russian sabotage: 'Put everything on the table'
lead: Russian sabotage takes place in the Netherlands much more often than is made public. According to minister Yeşilgöz, this is deliberately not publicised, so as not to make the Russians any wiser. Security experts question that strategy. "I am a strong advocate of putting as much out in the open as possible."

title: Máxima and Mathilde together at UN meeting in New York
lead: Queen Máxima attended the General Assembly of the United Nations in New York on Tuesday together with the Belgian Queen Mathilde. Photos show the two queens sitting next to each other in the assembly hall.

title: European Commission presents new procurement rules
lead: New European procurement rules are to make it easier for contracting authorities such as municipalities and provinces to put a contract out to the market. The European Commission made the long-awaited proposals for this public on Wednesday.

title: New chapter for Sugababes: original trio releases album
lead: The original members of the Sugababes are releasing a new album together for the first time in 26 years. Keisha Buchanan (41), Mutya Buena (41) and Siobhán Donaghy (42) announced on Instagram on Thursday that their new album will be released on 12 February.

title: Despite rain showers, the end of the drought is not yet in sight
lead: Inland shipping will probably suffer from low water levels in the rivers until early November. Arable farmers are also struggling with drought, although the biggest blows are already behind them.

title: Belastingdienst has no idea what its letters achieve
lead: Requests to file a tax return, reminders and letters about benefits. The Belastingdienst sends a wide arsenal of letters to citizens and businesses every year. A costly operation, but whether all those letters achieve their purpose is completely unclear.

title: The jailer had asked me in a cheerful tone whether I wanted to get off as soon as I entered the bunker
This is why the radical right and left are gaining more and more ground in Germany
lead: Germany was known as a country of stability. It was often the same parties that called the shots, a chancellor often stayed for at least a decade and the economy ran as if by itself. But something has changed with the eastern neighbours. The radical-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) is gaining more and more ground and yesterday won a state election for the second time. On the other side, the socialist Die Linke is also growing.

title: Mayor of Heumen: extreme violence is a national problem
lead: Mayor <entity id="person:joerie-minses">Joerie Minses</entity> of the Gelderland municipality of Heumen has called on <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> to tackle serious crime. He did so at the start of the first municipal council meeting since the mass violence in Overasselt, which falls under the municipality of Heumen. The meeting also briefly paused to reflect on the death of the security guard.

title: Utrecht municipalities voice concerns about provincial nitrogen plan
lead: Four municipalities have voiced their concerns to the <entity id="org:provincie-utrecht">provincie Utrecht</entity> about the provincial plan for the rural area. In a letter to Provinciale Staten, the municipalities of <entity id="org:gemeente-leusden">Leusden</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-woudenberg">Woudenberg</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-rhenen">Rhenen</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-renswoude">Renswoude</entity> write that the nitrogen measures lead to uncertainty and unrest among farmers and other parties involved, and that trust in the government is declining as a result.

title: Finally, some drama and emotion in European politics
lead: National politics has Prinsjesdag, with the carriage, the throne, the fashion show and the pathetic hat selfies that go viral on Instagram. In exactly the same way, European politics now has SOTEU.

title: Yeşilgöz warns: 'Russian sabotage much more often than you think'
lead: The drones above military base Volkel are certainly not the only sabotage action the Russians may have been behind, says defence minister Yesilgöz. "Much more happens than you know", she says. But in many cases little publicity is given to it so as not to make the enemy any wiser.

title: Almost sixteen years in prison demanded on appeal in 'abortion murder' case
lead: On Thursday, on appeal, the OM demanded a prison sentence of fifteen years and nine months and tbs with compulsory treatment against Dennis van E. He was previously convicted of the murder of his unborn child and the fatal assault of the mother.

title: Reporters from CNN, Politico and MS NOW refused at White House, despite court ruling
lead: Reporters from the news media CNN, Politico and MS NOW (formerly MSNBC) have been barred from the White House, despite a court ruling a few hours earlier that the ban…

title: René Froger's illness causes uncertainty about future of Toppers: 'He is in charge there'
lead: René Froger (65) announced last week that because of an autoimmune disease he is forced to cancel his performances, including his anniversary show in Ahoy. Although the disease is not life-threatening and treatment and improvement are possible, it is currently still unclear how his further recovery will go. And so the question also arises: what now for De Toppers?

title: Sleep like a pro

lead: Going by the title, you might expect a cheerful, light summery piece of music.
