title: Journalists from CNN, MS Now and Politico have access to the White House again
Mourinho critical of refereeing after defeat to Atlético
lead: MADRID (ANP/RTR) - Real Madrid coach José Mourinho was angry with the refereeing on Sunday after the defeat to Atlético Madrid (2-1). During a press conference he showed a photo of two fouls that Atlético players committed in the first half and for which they were not punished.

title: Santje (63) built a tiny house in Waterland: 'Here I only hear the birds, some lowing of the cows and the cackling of the geese'
News channels strike back: Trump boycotted at press event
lead: News channels in America are angry with Donald Trump. Last week the president barred CNN and two other news organisations from the White House. Trump thinks they are too critical and spread fake news. In response, other media decided to boycott a press event by Trump.

title: Police dogs and riot police: far-right protest in Den Haag gets out of hand
lead: Footage shows unrest on and around the Malieveld in Den Haag at a demonstration by, among others, right-wing extremists. Demonstrators used violence and threw fireworks.

title: Cloud predominates, sun shows itself now and then
lead: Today's weather is characterised by a lot of cloud. In the northwestern half there is occasionally some light rain or drizzle. Tomorrow the day starts with some rain, mainly in the southeast. Otherwise we see sun alternating with cumulus clouds.

title: New subsidy scheme for second-hand electric cars is 'prone to fraud'
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> hopes to open the new subsidy scheme with which lower incomes can buy a second-hand electric car this year. The government accepts that, according to implementing body <entity id="org:rijksdienst-voor-ondernemend-nederland">RVO</entity>, it may encourage fraud and improper use. Meanwhile, interested parties hope they will qualify for the support.

title: The repression continues in Venezuela, with a touch of freedom at Trump's request

'I am grateful that we are such a close-knit family, we really got through this loss together'
lead: Michael Huijser and Esther Huijser-Driessen both work in the cultural sector. They got to know each other as neighbours in the Amsterdam Jordaan. "When I went to live there, a friend already said to me: you are getting a very nice neighbour."

title: Partner wants to release unreleased music by Ben Saunders
lead: Janita Engels, the partner of the late singer and tattoo artist Ben Saunders, plans to share new music by Ben in the future. 'Music that he worked on with so much passion recently and that was incredibly important to him', Janita writes on Instagram.

title: Troonrede 2026
lead: On 15 September 2026 <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity> opened the new working year of parliament in the Koninklijke Schouwburg in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity> by delivering the King's Speech. Below you will find the text of the King's Speech.

title: Which artist wants to go to the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest for the Netherlands? This name is going around
lead: After long deliberation, the <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> has finally made the decision on participation in the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest: the Netherlands will simply take part again next year.

title: In the reorganisation, Amazon did not have to come up with hard figures
lead: The works council of two Dutch divisions of the Amazon group gave advice on a proposed reorganisation that would make dozens of employees in the Netherlands redundant. The reorganisation decision deviated from the advice, and Amazon did not come up with hard figures. The Ondernemingskamer does not see this as an obstacle.

title: From gummies to pills: how desirable are sleep aids for children?
lead: Parents of children who have difficulty falling asleep can easily get melatonin and so-called sleep gummies at drugstores and web shops. This is shown by research by Editie NL. Yet a new youth healthcare guideline advises against their use in children in most cases.

title: Defender Huijsen back in squad of world champions Spain
lead: Spain's national coach Luis de la Fuente has included Dean Huijsen in the national squad again. The Real Madrid defender, who was born in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity> but grew up in Spain, missed the World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico due to a muscle injury. Spain became world champions there.

title: After three years, doubts about effect of Wet goed verhuurderschap
lead: It is now more than three years since the Wet goed verhuurderschap came into force, after the bill had been steered through both Kamers by then minister of Housing Hugo de Jonge. The law was, among other things, a response to the report Geen tweederangsburgers, in which the commissie-Roemer called attention to the living conditions of labour migrants.

title: Restless griffier Remco Nehmelman goes to serve the king
lead: Remco Nehmelman made the Eerste Kamer an 'earthquake-proof' organisation. Now he is moving to the Kabinet van de Koning to support <entity id="person:willem-alexander">Willem-Alexander</entity>.

title: Monique Hansler draws striking conclusion about her cat's love life
lead: Monique Hansler would like to find a companion for cat Tammy, but she does set a striking condition. According to Monique, Tammy is gay, and so his future boyfriend must be of the same sex. 'De Hanslers: van de Piste naar de Playa' can be seen every Monday at 20:30 on SBS6.

title: BNNVARA takes documentary 'Verstoten vaders' offline; prosecution demands 24 months against main character
lead: The film Verstoten vaders has been taken offline after it became known that lead Armand S. is being prosecuted for intimate terrorism. The OM describes a pattern of stalking and coercive control over a "very long period".

title: Higher asset threshold for remission costs millions, but yields little
lead: A higher upper limit for the remission of local taxes will not necessarily lead to a decrease in the number of people in debt assistance. The tax benefit it gives them is out of all proportion to residents' possible debt burden. An increase does, however, cost municipalities tens of millions of euros in missed tax revenue.

title: When your buddy suddenly becomes your manager
lead: For years you work well together, and then suddenly that nice colleague becomes your manager. How do you deal with that? What should you definitely do and not do?

title: England sees five players drop out for upcoming international break
lead: LONDEN (ANP/RTR) - England national coach Thomas Tuchel cannot call on Cole Palmer, Declan Rice, Marcus Rashford, Tino Livramento and Kobbie Mainoo for the upcoming internationals. The five have withdrawn injured for the Nations League matches against Spain, Czech Republic, Croatia and Czech Republic again.

title: The Netherlands captivated by new 'adviser' to Sinterklaas: 'Can it be a woman?'
lead: It will be a while yet before the lovely evening has come, but our hearts are already beating full of expectation. Since Stefan de Walle (61) announced a few days ago that he is stopping as Sinterklaas's assistant, rumours have been buzzing about who will succeed him. Names of well-known Dutch people are being thrown around freely.

title: Dissolving the body after death (resomation) moves closer: 'Still a great many question marks'
lead: Having your body dissolved in a chemical liquid after your death: it is called resomation and looks set to become possible soon. <entity id="org:ministerraad">De ministerraad</entity> will soon take a decision on it. Funeral directors are already getting questions about it, but what such a farewell will look like in practice is still far from clear.

title: 'AI objections delay housebuilding'
lead: Objections that were presumably drafted with artificial intelligence are leading to delays in construction. BNR Nieuwsradio and trade journal Cobouw reported this after a round of municipalities, developers and other parties in construction.

title: Whoever sings for the Netherlands in Bulgaria, staying silent about Gaza will not be an option
Revival of the war threatens in Ethiopia
Municipalities ask for policy room, money and feasible tasks
lead: Sufficient policy room and financial resources and feasible tasks. Only then can municipalities carry out social tasks well. The VNG writes this in a position paper to the Tweede Kamer for the debate 'strengthening decentralised government' taking place this afternoon. 'These preconditions must always be taken into account in new legislation and policy.'

title: Lawyer for family of Kimberly (23), who died: witnesses saw she was not driving
lead: The lawyer assisting the family of 23-year-old Kimberly, the Rotterdam woman who died on Aruba, says that several witnesses to the accident have come forward. They state that Kimberly was not driving the off-road vehicle, whereas Aruban media did report that she was. The surviving relatives have 'serious doubts about the quality of the official investigation'.

title: Volgend weekend geen treinen naar Amsterdam Centraal
lead: Spoorbeheerder ProRail heeft aangekondigd dat er op zaterdag 3 oktober geen treinen van of naar Amsterdam Centraal rijden...

title: Roma from De Bondgenoten undergoes emergency surgery: 'A shock when I ended up in ICU'
lead: Roma Grasso (26), known from 'De Bondgenoten', has had a rough weekend. The reality star was rushed to hospital because of a throat infection and had to be operated on immediately. On Instagram she says that she is now back home, but the shock has not yet worn off.

title: Gen Z stays away from elections in Morocco, despite earlier protests
lead: A year after the Gen Z protests in their country, Moroccans go to the polls today. Turnout is particularly low among young people. "Many young Moroccans have given up hope that things will get better and that they will find homes and jobs after all", says correspondent Sophie van Leeuwen.

title: Macron had 'good conversation' with Trump about Ukraine: 'He was accommodating'
lead: French President Emmanuel Macron told reporters that he had a 'very good and very constructive' conversation with American President Donald Trump about Ukraine. "We talked at length about Ukraine and Russia, about the need to help our Ukrainian friends faster and better with missile defence systems."

title: Liz arrested after defrauding B&B Vol Liefde star Robert Jan
lead: Liz, who appeared last season in 'Kees van der Spek Ontmaskert', has been arrested in Scotland. Kees van der Spek (62) says this on Instagram, and according to him it is confirmed by the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity>. Liz, who among others defrauded Robert Jan from 'B&B Vol Liefde', fled to Scotland while she still had to serve a prison sentence in the Netherlands.

'This is a war that everyone saw coming': fighting in Tigray threatens to escalate into wider regional conflict
lead: A new war has broken out in northern Ethiopia. The fighting is more than a local uprising in the province of Tigray. The capture of three airfields and fighting with the federal army could be the start of a much broader confrontation with <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> of prime minister Abiy Ahmed.

title: New details about Presley Gerber's death: staff member found him in rehab clinic
lead: Presley Gerber, the son of Cindy Crawford (60) and brother of top model Kaia Gerber (25), died on Sunday at the age of 27. He died in a rehab clinic in Los Angeles.

title: Seniors arrested for destroying traffic light over conspiracy theory
lead: In Ilfracombe, England, seniors were recently arrested for vandalising a traffic light. The vandalism is not an isolated case: in several English cities traffic lights are being deliberately destroyed because of a remarkable conspiracy theory.

title: Minister confirms: hospitals to perform late abortions more frequently
Does armpit and beard hair grow back faster if you shave it?

lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> is demanding twelve years in prison for Jim B., a former civil servant of the municipality of Amsterdam. He allegedly sold data from the municipal systems. That data was allegedly then used for at least 95 violent incidents.

title: National coach Xavi gets the question: 'Are you going to learn our national anthem?'
lead: In his press conference, national coach Xavi Hernández explains his selection of 26 players that he has put together for the upcoming international break, and looks ahead to this first phase with Oranje. When he is asked whether he is going to learn the Dutch national anthem, he says: "I promised Marianne (director KNVB), but I need time."

title: Fake model scout Dogukan B. flees from Alberto Stegeman
lead: Fraudster Dogukan B. was previously exposed by 'Undercover in Nederland' and later convicted by the court, but turns out to have simply continued his practices. In the latest episode, Alberto Stegeman (55) and victim Leida once again confront the fake model scout with the vulgar way in which he operates.

title: In pictures: riot police deployed at protest against possible arrival of asylum centre in Opheusden
lead: In Opheusden in Gelderland there was a demonstration last night at the town hall, where a meeting was being held about the possible arrival of an asylum seekers' centre. The atmosphere turned grim and the riot police (ME) had to be deployed. At least ten people were arrested.

title: Van de Zandschulp puts Davis Cup team 1-0 up with difficulty
lead: Botic van de Zandschulp has put the Dutch tennis team ahead against Colombia in the Davis Cup. In the Maaspoort in Den Bosch, he won the first match of the tie against Johan Alexander Rodriguez in three sets with considerable difficulty: 4-6 6-1 7-5.

title: Raphinha helps Barcelona past Sevilla with hat-trick
lead: Captain Raphinha has helped leaders FC Barcelona to a 3-1 win at Sevilla. The Brazilian international accounted for the Catalans' entire output.

lead: Now that it is finally clear that the Netherlands is taking part in the Song Contest, there is plenty of room for a new national discussion: who will be Sinterklaas's new assistant? title: Biodiesel for ships now cheaper than regular marine fuel
lead: The price of biodiesel for shipping in the port of <entity id="org:gemeente-rotterdam">Rotterdam</entity> is cheaper than regular gas oil for ships for the first time.

lead: Er is olie gevonden op meerdere stranden in Zeeland, heeft het provinciebestuur gewaarschuwd.

title: Shortage of civil servants leaves its mark everywhere
lead: Whether you put a small municipality or a large city under the magnifying glass: the shortage of civil servants leaves its mark everywhere, both in services to residents and in policy implementation (<entity id="org:uitvoering-van-beleid">uitvoering van beleid</entity>).

"The brain injury I sustained was quite serious, so a lot of rehabilitation is still needed", said the singer. "There is a long, hard road ahead of me, but I am fighting to get better."

title: Edwin Evers shares memory of last visit to Bartina Koeman: 'Thank you for everything'
lead: Edwin Evers (55) reflects on the death of Bartina Koeman in his radio show. Edwin has been good friends with Ronald (63) and Bartina for many years and responds to the sad news in 'Evers & Co.'. In the broadcast he takes ample time to remember her.

title: Bees show how drones can land on difficult terrain
lead: Bees can land effortlessly on a moving flower. Researchers from <entity id="org:gemeente-wageningen">Wageningen</entity> University & Research and TU Delft are looking at the insect to teach drones to land better on difficult surfaces.

title: No indexation of gemeentefonds phase-in model in 2028 either
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> will also not apply indexation in the recalibration of the gemeentefonds in 2028. The cabinet decided this 'for the sake of traceability and explainability'.

Gary Lineker would never have attacked Virgil van Dijk like that
Anouk's relationship drove Diederik in De Bondgenoten to despair: 'She still had a boyfriend and that hurt'
lead: His love for Anouk left Diederik quite confused during his participation in 'De Bondgenoten'. While he developed feelings for her, she was still in a relationship. In his new column for RTL Boulevard, Diederik tells how hard that uncertainty was for him, why he still kept coming back to Anouk and when he finally dared to fully let his feelings in.

title: Brazen and ruthless: bunq boss Ali Niknam tried to outdo competitor ING with harassment. 'Fuck you very much'
lead: He became successful through a combination of genius, brazenness and a ruthless management style. As in 2023, when he hijacked the name of bunq's new chatbot from the big ING. On Tuesday NRC publishes an unauthorised biography of bunq boss Ali Niknam, one of the richest entrepreneurs in the Netherlands.

title: First one and a half billion from the nitrogen fund released
lead: The agriculture ministry is putting most of the 20 billion euros that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>-Jetten has reserved for the nitrogen approach up to and including 2035 into the new Fonds voor stikstof, landbouw en natuur. Next year the ministry will spend the first 1.5 billion euros of this.

title: Davina Michelle, Waylon or Ilse DeLange to the song contest? 'I am not saying a wholehearted yes to taking part right now'
lead: The <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> is breathing new life into the Eurovision Song Contest, but the search for a candidate will be quite complicated. Who dares? lead: The UK already did what the Netherlands is now considering: granting a large subsidy for making a Tata steel plant greener. Dutch critics fear that here too it will not stop at a single gift.

title: Jury deeply moved by performance of choir of cancer survivors in Got Talent: 'What an honour that you are standing here'

title: VNG board advises against 'grip on asylum flow' motion

title: Knokke Off gets a film sequel: filming started in three countries
lead: Filming of 'Knokke Off: De film' started on Wednesday, Netflix reports. According to the streaming service, the film, the sequel to the popular series 'Knokke Off', will be released in 2027. Filming is taking place in Belgium, France and Thailand, among other places.

title: Beautiful tribute: Koeman junior in tears during applause for late mother
lead: An emotional moment during AZ-Telstar. In the twelfth minute the match was stopped for a tribute to Bartina Koeman, the mother of Telstar goalkeeper Ronald Koeman junior, who died on Tuesday. The keeper could not hold back his tears.

title: Sc Heerenveen earns second win of the season at Sparta
lead: Sc Heerenveen has earned its second win of the season. The side from <entity id="org:provincie-fryslan">Friesland</entity> beat Sparta <entity id="org:gemeente-rotterdam">Rotterdam</entity> 4-0 at Het Kasteel.

title: Family and football world say goodbye to Bartina Koeman in Laren
lead: Family, close friends and many friends, mainly from the football world, said goodbye to Bartina Koeman today. Last Tuesday the wife of coach Ronald Koeman (63) died at the age of 65 as a result of breast cancer. In Laren this afternoon her sparkling life was remembered in an impressive way.

title: Justice minister Van Weel eats humble pie after confusion over unprocessed police reports: 'I take this to heart'
Astrid Holleeder shines as guest editor-in-chief at Margriet: 'I was always that grey mouse'
lead: Astrid Holleeder is guest editor-in-chief of 'Margriet' this month, a role with a special meaning for her. Her mother always used to read the magazine, while Astrid herself is no longer the 'grey mouse' she once was and increasingly dares to be herself.

title: In the sixth year Bloem (22) texted Lou (21) that she had feelings for him: 'I didn't really know how to answer'
Lily Collins says final goodbye to her role in Emily in Paris: 'I am speechless'
lead: Lily Collins (37) has officially said goodbye to the character Emily Cooper from the long-running Netflix series 'Emily in Paris'. On Friday she had her last shoot for the series, which ends after six seasons.

title: Transport operator fears for public transport in the province of Utrecht
lead: Transport operator Keolis fears that providing public transport in the province of Utrecht will become unsustainable in the long term. The company and the province are examining how the public transport concession Utrecht Buiten (the bus service in <entity id="org:gemeente-amersfoort">Amersfoort</entity> and in the east and west of the province) can 'remain reliable, accessible and financially sustainable' in the long term, a spokeswoman confirms following reporting by de Volkskrant.

title: Closing Time | Twisted Teens
lead: Twisted Teens from New Orleans has something of the early Kings of Leon. Simple but catchy rock songs, guitars with a modest dose of overdrive, with a pleasant southern feel. All according to the old recipe of Creedence Clearwater Revival. The steel guitar is a special addition, though I do not rule out that Creedence also […] Read more posts on Sargasso

title: Trump backs ban on export of diesel
lead: In the run-up to the midterm elections in November, the president is trying to get the price of diesel down. It has risen sharply since the start of the war against Iran.

title: With 'Verbied dit boek' this writer challenged Trump's America. And indeed: his book was banned
René Froger makes painful decision and cancels anniversary show
lead: The anniversary show 'Show of the Year 2026' by René Froger (65) in <entity id="org:gemeente-rotterdam">Rotterdam</entity> Ahoy in December will not go ahead. The singer announced this, after the earlier announcement that he has been diagnosed with the autoimmune disease polymyositis. In this disease the immune system attacks the muscles.

title: Belgian navy seeks alternative to Damen frigates
lead: The Belgian navy has taken a new concrete step towards replacing Damen Shipyards for the construction of two frigates. With that, the sky above the Dutch shipbuilder has grown somewhat darker again.

title: Not being able to say goodbye to brother left its mark on Carrie ten Napel
lead: As a child, Carrie ten Napel (46) was not allowed to say goodbye to her deceased brother. Her parents wanted to protect her by doing so, but that choice stayed with her. In 'De Kist' the presenter tells how this experience has influenced her view of death.

title: New details about Stuntkabouter's fatal accident: drove too fast and under the influence
lead: News in the case surrounding Stuntkabouter, or Martijn van Eijzeren (28). Four months ago he was involved in an accident in France, in which his friend and director Ilya Vierhout (28) was killed. Since then Martijn has had to stay in France because of the investigation. Sources close to the investigation confirm to RTL Boulevard on Monday that Martijn drove too fast and was under the influence of drugs.

title: The same loop 1,381 times already, all the way around the IJsselmeer
lead: Kees Stavenuiter (73) has already cycled around the IJsselmeer 1,381 times, a route of 200 kilometres that holidaymakers often take a week to complete. Kees rides it in a day, rain or shine. "At the thousandth lap they were waiting for me with cake."

title: Childcare benefit is being scrapped: from 2029 on, childcare will be much cheaper
Tribute to the late Stan after Miljoenenjacht raises questions: this is what he meant to the programme
lead: After an evening on which contestant Sjoerd severely tested the nerves of 'Miljoenenjacht' viewers, the broadcast suddenly came to a subdued end. A black-and-white photo of the late Stan Schrederhof appeared on screen, but no explanation followed. Viewers were therefore left with the same question: who was he?

title: A crisis and recovery act for grid congestion is now on its way
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> wants to drastically shorten the lead time of electricity grid expansions by scrapping or simplifying permit procedures. 'Expanding the electricity grid now takes far too much time', state secretary Jo-Annes de Bat of Climate and Green Growth said on Friday. 'We simply cannot afford that.' After <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity> he announced new legislation along the lines of the Crisis- en herstelwet.

title: Coalition deal on WIA, purchasing power and box 3 must win over opposition
lead: Insiders expect that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> can accommodate opposition parties on three themes on Friday. That starts a new round of negotiations on the budget.

title: In this 'Tetris hotel', container units form homes on the water
lead: Entire residential areas on the water: it sounds like something futuristic, but a small-scale version already exists in <entity id="org:gemeente-leeuwarden">Leeuwarden</entity>. In the so-called 'Tetris hotel' you can stay overnight in container units that can be linked together and so take on the shape of the iconic game Tetris.

title: Frankfurt is even popularly called 'Crackfurt': 'This will become the biggest drug problem in Europe'
Atlético win city derby against Real Madrid 2-1
lead: Atlético Madrid won the city derby against Real Madrid 2-1 on Sunday. Coach Diego Simeone's team thereby overtook Real Madrid in the standings. After seven matches, Atlético are in second place with 16 points behind FC Barcelona. José Mourinho's Real Madrid have 15 points.

title: 7 years in prison demanded for suspect of fatal explosion in Rotterdam
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> is demanding 7 years in prison for 37-year-old Jalal O., the suspect of the fatal explosion on the Schammenkamp in Rotterdam. Three people were killed. O. is on trial for making and processing cocaine and for deliberately causing the deadly explosion.

title: Children of Andy van der Meijde and Melisa Schaufeli steal the show again in new season of reality soap
lead: The reality series 'Andy & Melisa' returns after a year. Life for the two in <entity id="org:gemeente-apeldoorn">Apeldoorn</entity> is still busy, busy, busy, and since this week you can see exactly what they and the children have been up to in the meantime.

title: Meta takes Roel Maalderink's critical video about Meta AI glasses offline
lead: A critical video about Meta's AI glasses has been removed from the platforms Facebook and Instagram. In the video, Dutch programme maker Roel Maalderink wore filming Meta glasses to visit the company's office in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity> to film colleagues.

title: Jan Slagter does not want to be on the song contest team: 'Then I'll send Sieneke'
lead: Jan Slagter (72) sees no role for Omroep MAX in the independent team of experts that will consider the Dutch song contest entry. The broadcaster's boss also does not want to sit on a selection committee himself, he said on Wednesday in the RTL 4 talk show 'Renze'.

title: Expert in international criminal law Göran Sluiter (1970-2026) preferred to remain modest
Jetten responds to anonymous criticism from within cabinet: 'Leaks biggest annoyance'
lead: This week the AD published an article in which cabinet members anonymously criticised the leadership style of prime minister Jetten. Political reporter Frits Wester asks Jetten during his weekly press conference whether this was discussed today in <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity>. "As we do every Friday, we did a short round", says Jetten.

title: How minimal are the minima?
lead: It used to be called poor relief. Nowadays we speak of minimabeleid (policy for people on minimum incomes). It is a typically municipal task. Cities and villages were already doing it in the Middle Ages. And yet we knew much less about it than we thought.

title: Cabinet allocates hundreds of millions extra for security
lead: The ministry is allocating 231 million euros extra for security for 2027. From 2030 that amount rises to 462 million euros. More community police officers is an important spearhead, according to the Miljoenennota.

title: Olivia, Damian and Sarah died in school camp tragedy: 'They are now together forever'
lead: They were twelve years old: Olivia, Sarah and Damian. They were killed last June in Vogelwaarde in Zeeland when a car drove into them while they were cycling. The school principal with whom they were on school camp also died. The bereaved families are speaking out for the first time. Sarah's mother speaks on their behalf in an interview with RTL Nieuws.

title: Nederlandse Digitale Dienst takes shape
lead: The Nederlandse Digitale Dienst, the 'technical service' of central government, is becoming concrete. The Dienst now consists of around 45 people, coming from Digilab, Forum Standaardisatie and Bureau Architectuur, among others. Together they are working on three 'breakthrough projects', including a private government cloud.

title: Batavia makes last journey over the water, goes to Amsterdam for maintenance
lead: The ship De Batavia, a replica of the VOC ship, departed from <entity id="org:gemeente-lelystad">Lelystad</entity> this morning and is being towed to Amsterdam. There the ship will go into dry dock and be fitted with a steel support structure.

title: Why does Donald Trump hate nature?
lead: Trump is taking the knife to large pieces of protected nature area in Utah. Peter and Karlijn talk with science journalists Sjoerd de Jong and Marcel aan de Brugh about the political…

title: A bridge, a tunnel: what does Amsterdam actually want with the leap across the IJ?
Monique Hansler adopts injured shelter cat Balou: 'I could cry'
lead: In 'De Hanslers: van de Piste naar de Playa' the Hansler family is looking for a companion for cat Tammie. In the shelter, tomcat Balou immediately makes an impression on Monique. He has been through a serious accident and several operations. That history does not leave her unmoved.

title: Defender Malacia continues football career at FC Cincinnati
lead: Tyrell Malacia is continuing his football career in the United States. The 27-year-old left wing-back has signed a contract with FC Cincinnati until the summer of 2027.

title: Loretta Schrijver remains 'present' during recordings of The Masked Singer
lead: Last year Loretta Schrijver died, who for years was a familiar face on Dutch television and was part of 'The Masked Singer', among other things. Her death was a great loss for the Netherlands, but certainly also for her colleagues on the popular family programme. Although Loretta is no longer here, her presence still seems to be felt in the studio of 'The Masked Singer'.

title: Princess Diana's brother makes his sister human again in book: 'One big love letter'
lead: Almost thirty years after the death of Princess Diana, her younger brother Charles Spencer (62) records his memories of her. In 'Swan Song: Diana, My Sister', which will be published in the Netherlands on Tuesday with the title 'Zwanenzang', he writes not only about the world-famous style icon, but above all about the sister he knew: funny, caring and always willing to support him. Royalty watcher Annemarie de Kunder has already read the book and discusses the highlights.

title: Daughter of influencer Valerie Gumster fell down the stairs: 'I have failed as a mother'
lead: The worries are piling up for influencer Valerie Gumster (32), better known online as Closet van Val, and her husband Edwin. Their daughter Luna has been at home for quite some time, suffered from her medication and also got a concussion after a hard fall down the stairs. Meanwhile, the family is confronted on social media with nasty stories about the girl.

title: 'De waanzinnige boomhut' illustrator deliberately made his drawings look clumsy
Notable names in Xavi's Oranje squad: Veerman and Zechiël in, no Depay
lead: Xavi Hernández has announced his first squad as national coach of the Dutch national team. It contains a few notable names: Ruben van Bommel (PSV) and Gjivai Zechiël (Feyenoord), for example, have been called up. Joey Veerman returns. Memphis Depay has not been selected.

title: Gemeentefonds approaches 50 billion, but threat of cliff remains
lead: The size of the gemeentefonds rises next year to almost 50 billion euros. But after that peak year the financial cliff still awaits: in 2028 there is 2.7 billion euros less in the pot, and in 2029 another 1.2 billion euros less.

title: SoftBank turns investments in AI into an expensive adventure
lead: The Japanese tech investor still manages to raise a lot of money from the market in order to invest in OpenAI, among others. But this does come at a price: a high interest rate.

title: Heroic rescue in China: student saves man from steep rock face
lead: A Chinese man who was stuck on a rock face has been rescued by a 25-year-old student. Because of exhaustion the man could no longer climb any further and was in danger of slipping off at a height of about 30 metres.

title: Tony Junior is frustrated that relationships do not last: 'I would really like to become a dad'
lead: Tony Junior (36) longs for a steady relationship and hopes eventually to start a family. In 'Podcast De Podcast' the DJ says that his relationships regularly break down and that he wonders why it just won't work out. His wish for children is not new in any case: by his own account he has wanted to become a father since he was twelve.

title: What are the effects of meditation? Should you make a habit of it? And how? Experts answer
lead: Autumn brings shorter days, a lack of sunlight and many obligations. Perhaps you would benefit from meditation in this period. What exactly is it? And how do you make a habit of it? Experts answer.

title: Paul Haenen sets the bar high for new voice of Bert: 'Has to moan a bit'
lead: After more than fifty years, Paul Haenen (80) is saying goodbye as the voice of Bert from 'Sesamstraat', after his regular counterpart Wim T. Schippers died this past June. In 'De Coen & Sander Show' on JOE, Paul tells what requirements a new voice must meet, and the men speak with Bert for the last time.

title: Lucille Werner's parents saw a different future for her: 'Just become a secretary'
lead: Lucille Werner (58) has not let herself be held back by the expectations of others in her life. The former 'Lingo' presenter, who was born with brain damage and therefore walks with more difficulty, tells Libelle that even her parents would rather have seen a modest career for her. Meanwhile she herself dreamed of working in television.

title: 538 newsreader Florentien van der Meulen has married: 'Everything was right'
lead: Radio newsreader Florentien van der Meulen (55) married her partner Emile last weekend. "It was so idyllic and fairytale-like", Florentien said on Monday in the morning show of Radio 538.

title: Von der Leyen: 'We must accelerate drastically'
lead: In the State of the Union in the European Parliament in Strasbourg on Wednesday, President of the European Commission Ursula von der Leyen put the emphasis on speed. 'We must move much faster', she said. 'We must accelerate drastically.' She called AI one of the tipping points of our time, alongside climate change, decisive for the future.

title: Still grey and cloudy for now, but temperatures up to 25 degrees at the weekend
lead: A high-pressure area is bringing extremely calm weather. The air present is humid and that shows itself today in grey weather, with a chance of a spot of drizzle in the north. Tomorrow the day may start with fog locally in the west.

title: Acute shortage of prison staff: DJI expects to have 30 percent fewer staff in ten years, so regime becomes more austere
lead: Structurally too few cells and too few prison guards: that has consequences. Dutch prisons must work in a way that needs "fewer staff", with "open living spaces", ankle monitors and an austere regime. In the coming years the existing staff shortage will increase even further.

title: Defender Timber available for Oranje against Germany
lead: Jurriën Timber will be part of the matchday squad of the Netherlands team on Thursday for the home match against Germany in the Nations League. National coach Xavi Hernández said this at a press conference on Wednesday.

title: The hollyhocks hang in an arc over the pavement, there is no one to tie them up
lead: NRC asked photographers to capture the summer close to home. What happens if you take the familiar as a starting point? Olivier Middendorp from <entity id="org:gemeente-haarlem">Haarlem</entity> photographed the "languid atmosphere" that takes over his neighbourhood during the summer holidays. Until the first ordinary Monday approaches and the handheld vacuum cleaner comes out.

title: US violates obligations as UN host country by refusing visas for Palestinian delegation, Palestinian president Abbas rails in video message
lead: The US already has a military base in the northwest of Greenland and is getting two more, according to the Greenland deal, about which more details came out on Tuesday. This agreement differs from earlier deals in that there is now attention for the interests of Greenland itself.

title: Observing
lead: I have a new hobby. What am I saying: a new obsession. I observe. From the bench in my small city garden I take photos of little plants and little animals. The Houtpantserjuffer. Tijmereprijs. A Gehakkelde Aurelia, the Grote Brandnetel, the Boomblauwtje and a Venstersectorspin.

title: A healthy market deserves a healthy market master
lead: The <entity id="org:zbo-autoriteit-consument-en-markt">ACM</entity> is getting new powers. It is good to keep checking whether supervision is still up to date or needs to be modernised.

title: PSV coach Bosz expects 'tough away match' at FC Twente
lead: PSV coach Peter Bosz regards next Sunday's away match against FC Twente as a top match. "In a very short time that will be yet another tough away match for us. FC Twente are on a good run, so we have work to do", the coach of the Eredivisie leaders said in the run-up to the match in <entity id="org:gemeente-enschede">Enschede</entity>. "It is the last match before a long international break, so then we have to win. Otherwise we will be stuck with that for three weeks."

title: Is Ramsey Nasr the new Sinterklaas? NTR reveals nothing
lead: The NTR is not responding to the rumours about the new Sinterklaas. The Instagram channel Sinttalk says on Wednesday evening that it knows with 95 percent certainty that Ramsey Nasr (52) is succeeding Stefan de Walle (61) as the good saint in the Sinterklaasjournaal and the national arrival.

title: The country's oldest newspaper deliverer (90) is stopping: 'Cannot sit still'
lead: Ten years ago Hendrik Tahapary (90) had two wishes: to become the oldest newspaper deliverer in the Netherlands and to turn 100, so that the mayor would come to visit. He is now probably the oldest newspaper deliverer in the Netherlands, but he is not yet 100. Still, the <entity id="pos:burgemeester-arnhem">burgemeester van Arnhem</entity>, <entity id="person:ahmed-marcouch">Ahmed Marcouch</entity>, came to visit him. "It was so much more than delivering newspapers."

title: Janneke's daughter got leukaemia: 'Mum, am I going to die? I could not give her the answer'
lead: On 9 September 2026 it was four years since her daughter was diagnosed with leukaemia. After two years of chemotherapy, mountains of pills, 25 blood transfusions, nasty side effects and carrying on, Jasmijn grew into a strong girl full of zest for life, a survivor.

title: After starting 'Dag lieverds' I did not want to put the book down, I finished it that same day
lead: Columnist Frits Abrahams read the book Dag lieverds, ik ga nu slapen by Peter Brusse. The book is about the last two and a half years of the life of his wife, who had ALS. "To process his grief, he visits the places where they were happy together. Out of fear of a breakdown, I would not have done that."

title: What makes a song sexy?
Police undercover operations are still too much 'quicksand', says this researcher. Because: how far do you go? 'Do you kiss someone if you have a wife?'
lead: Officers who work under cover live in two worlds. PhD candidate Sophie Naber argues for more dialogue among undercover officers and between them and their supervisors. "Do you kiss someone while you have a wife at home?"

title: British public rallies behind King Charles for now after new Diana revelations: 'People believe the king'
lead: The British public has to wait until Tuesday to be able to read 'Swan Song', but the memoirs of Charles Spencer (62) about his sister Diana were already shared with the media under embargo on Monday. And so there is once again a lot of fuss about the already much-discussed book.

title: Cabinet argues for European age limit for social media
lead: The Netherlands, together with Spain, is sending proposals to the European Commission for introducing a European minimum age for social media and other relevant digital services. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> wants to introduce privacy-friendly age verification. Services can be exempted from the age limit if they demonstrably meet safety standards.

title: Simple comme bonjour: green beans the French way, so first boil, then braise
Over coffee at the Belastingdienst for personal help: 'Sometimes people come in crying and leave with a big smile'
Report warns: European Union will not be ready in time for defence against Russia
lead: The EU's rearmament is not going fast and effectively enough to reach its goal: to have a strong defence with sufficient deterrence in 2030. To counter the threat of Russian aggression, the pace must be stepped up. That is stated in an EU report drawn up for the EU heads of government. Follow all developments in the war in Ukraine in our live blog.

title: Trump wants to halt diesel exports to Europe: price threatens to rise sharply
lead: The American president Donald Trump wants to stop the export of diesel from the US to Europe for 90 days. Experts fear that if that does indeed happen, the diesel price in Europe will rise sharply. But such a ban will ultimately not be favourable for the US itself either, they think.

title: Brobbey drops out before half-time in Oranje match against Germany, Meerdink makes debut
lead: Brian Brobbey dropped out injured before half-time on Thursday for Oranje in the home match against Germany in the Nations League. In the Johan Cruijff ArenA the striker was replaced by debutant Mexx Meerdink.

title: We will have to get used to postponement
lead: Anyone who reads the coalition agreement Aan de slag of D66, VVD and CDA can hardly miss the message: the relationship between central government and the decentralised governments must improve. 'The success of this cabinet stands or falls with the willingness to work together with the Tweede and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity>, other tiers of government and civil society organisations', the government agreement reads. And: 'The relationship with the other tiers of government will have to be restored. Good intergovernmental relations are essential to the major...

title: Dikes in danger? These volunteers are already standing by
lead: What do you do when a dike gives way? At six places in the Netherlands, volunteers are practising reinforcing dikes. In doing so they lay down hundreds of sandbags as if it were a real crisis.

title: Municipalities to enforce football rules more strictly
lead: Municipalities are going to make more intensive use of rules and permits to prevent disturbances at football matches. That is one of the agreements made after consultation between the football association KNVB, the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity>, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, the ministry of Justice and municipalities.

title: Tim Senders and Kiki Bosman have become parents of a son: 'Magical baby bubble'
lead: Rusks with aniseed sprinkles for Tim Senders (36) and Kiki Bosman (31): the couple have welcomed their first son Solé Jo. On Instagram the new parents share a series of photos of the little one. They also say they are on cloud nine.

title: From gummies to pills: how desirable are sleep aids for children?
lead: Parents of children who have difficulty falling asleep can easily get melatonin and so-called sleep gummies at drugstores and web shops. Yet a new youth healthcare guideline advises against their use in children in most cases. An Editie NL reporter visited several shops and looked at how accessible these products still are.

title: Dave Roelvink loses first professional boxing match: 'Past 10 days were tough'
lead: Dave Roelvink (32) has lost his first professional boxing match. The influencer made his professional debut at 'Boxing Gladiators'. The fight against Renars Rusins (39) was hard-fought.

title: 'It seems as if the government is giving up the fight for accessibility'
lead: Only 5 percent of the websites and apps of the Dutch government meet the accessibility requirements. Meanwhile, accessibility expert Jules Ernst sees some government websites even getting worse. 'A regulator was already promised in 2024, but nothing is happening.'

title: Dave Roelvink speaks out about split with Marijn Kuipers: 'It is not easy'
lead: Dave Roelvink (32) steps into the ring this week at 'Glory: Boxing Gladiators III'. The match comes shortly after it became known that his engagement to Marijn Kuipers (26) has been broken off. Dave says during the press conference that, given the circumstances, he is doing 'okay'.

title: Households have slightly more to spend, mainly thanks to higher wages
lead: Dutch households had slightly more to spend in the second quarter of this year than in the same period a year earlier. This is mainly due to higher wages, higher benefits and the growth in the number of jobs.
